payload.text: 9 min is the pull point, not a guideline — protein-yogurt cookies keep cooking on the hot pan. Centers will look underdone; that's correct. They firm to a soft, cakey texture as they cool. Going past 10 min makes them dry and tight.
The 20–30 min chill is real work here — this dough has only 1 tbsp butter and barely spreads. Chilling firms it so the flattened mounds hold their shape; skipping it yields flat, patchy cookies.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.
Add the wet ingredients — egg, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla — and mix to a dough. If dry, add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.
Chill 20-30 min, then scoop onto a lined sheet, wet hands, and flatten (this dough barely spreads).
Bake at 350F for ~9 minutes — pull while the centers still look soft; they firm up as they cool.
Cool the cookies fully, then frost with the vanilla protein frosting (sub-recipe).

payload.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl - flour, cocoa, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.

Add the wet ingredients - egg, egg white, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla, the red gel coloring, and the vinegar - and mix to a dough. Cocoa makes this drier, so add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.

96124832-96e4-47a6-a05f-11a4e218139c.name: Vanilla Protein Cheesecake
96124832-96e4-47a6-a05f-11a4e218139c.description: Base protein cheesecake (vanilla SF pudding, pumpkin for moisture/body). Launch point for flavor variants. Low-fat / high-protein; pumpkin does the work fat does in a standard cheesecake. Tuned DENSE (Tier 1+2): pumpkin reduced 120->75g + 2 tbsp AP flour for a firmer set (AP because that's what's on hand — its gluten sets denser than cornstarch), baked DRY (no water bath) to a just-set center and chilled overnight — denser at near-zero macro cost (~129 cal/slice, ratio 9.1). Stays lean; if a bake comes out rubbery rather than densely creamy, add a little fat (more cream cheese or an extra yolk).
96124832-96e4-47a6-a05f-11a4e218139c.author: system

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients together — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder.
Add the wet ingredients (egg, egg white, melted butter, almond milk, vanilla) to the dry and mix to a dough.
Coat your hands in flour to make the dough easier to shape; divide into 5 cookies on a lined sheet.
Bake at 350F for 10 minutes.
Allow the cookies to cool fully before frosting.
Mix the Greek yogurt, SF vanilla pudding mix, vanilla, and a dash of salt into a frosting; spread on the cooled cookies (add sprinkles to taste).

notes.text: 10 minutes at 350F is the ceiling — with 3 scoops whey in only 5 cookies, these dry out fast. Pull when the edges are just set and the centers still look slightly underdone; carryover finishes them.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line an 8x8 pan. Mix the carrot, eggs, milk, Biscoff spread, Splenda, honey, vanilla, flour, protein, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until just combined; fold in the crushed Biscoff. Spread into the pan.
Bake 22-28 min until set. Let cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese smooth, then mix in the protein, milk, Splenda, and vanilla until fluffy and spreadable. Frost the cooled bars and top with crushed Biscoff. Cut into 12.

notes.text: 22 min is a starting check, not a target — with 90 g protein powder in an 8x8, the bars go from just-set to dry in a few minutes. Pull when a toothpick reads moist crumbs; the center will firm as it cools.

payload.instructionText: Beat the whole egg + egg white with the brown sugar only until the sugar dissolves and it looks smooth and glossy — then STOP. Chew and the shiny top come from dissolving, not air; don't whip it to a pale ribbon.
Whisk in the neutral oil, then the Greek yogurt.
Bloom the cocoa + espresso in a small splash of warm skim milk, then stir into the batter.

Whisk the flour + protein powder + salt, then fold in to no dry streaks, then ~10–15 extra strokes to develop a little gluten for chew — still stopping before it goes very stretchy or tough. No chocolate, no cornstarch.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the dry base — AP flour, whey protein, SF pudding mix, Splenda, baking powder, salt — until there are no protein clumps.
Add the melted butter, whole egg, Greek yogurt, and vanilla into the dry mix.
Stir to combine, then stop and let the bowl sit untouched 5 minutes so the whey and pudding starches swell into a shapeable dough. If still tacky, chill 5 more minutes.
Preheat oven/air fryer to 325F. Divide into 4 equal balls on parchment and press down firmly with your palm or a glass — this dough sets in the shape you give it, it won't spread.
Bake at 325F for 6-7 minutes. Pull the moment the edges look dry and set, even if the centers still look slightly soft — whey dries out fast.
Leave the cookies on the hot sheet 5-10 minutes; residual pan heat finishes the centers without making the protein rubbery.
Final step: rest in the fridge ~10 minutes to fully set, then eat.

steps.instructionText: Stir the cocoa, protein, espresso powder, oat flour, and salt together. Add the maple syrup, pumpkin, vanilla, and most of the milk and mix to a thick fudgy dough — add the rest of the milk a little at a time only if needed (a little goes a long way). Fold in the chocolate chips and melted butter.
Press the dough firmly into a parchment-lined loaf pan. Freeze 10 min (or refrigerate ~1 hr) until set, then slice into 8 bars. Store in the fridge.

notes.text: Add the 75 g milk gradually — with 3 scoops protein + 42 g oat flour, the dough tightens fast and a little milk goes a long way. Overshoot and the bars won't hold their shape after freezing.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 325F. Line a tray with parchment.
Whisk the wets - yogurt, pumpkin, egg, egg white, vanilla, food coloring, vinegar - then stir in the Splenda.
Add the dries - cocoa, oat flour, pudding, protein, baking soda, salt. Mix to a thick dough.
Rest 10-15 min to hydrate. If still batter-like, add oat flour 1 tbsp at a time until scoopable.
Scoop 5 cookies and shape into pucks (they barely spread). Bake 15-18 min at 325F until the tops spring back to a light touch and the edges are set.
Cool fully on the tray - they firm up as they cool.
Frost the cooled cookies with the protein cream-cheese frosting (see sub-recipe).

notes.text: The 10–15 min rest is necessary — oat flour hydrates slowly and the batter will look loose and unpipeable at first. Only add extra oat flour 1 tbsp at a time after the rest if it's still genuinely batter-like, not just soft.

steps.instructionText: Combine all the cake ingredients in a bowl and mix well.
Pour the batter evenly into two round cake molds.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
In a mixing bowl, combine the wet ingredients and mix.
In another mixing bowl, combine the dry ingredients and mix.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix and whisk thoroughly.
In a separate mixing bowl, combine the frosting ingredients and mix thoroughly.
In another separate mixing bowl, combine the filling ingredients and mix well.
Let the mixed frosting and mixed filling cool in the refrigerator while the donuts are cooking and resting.
Spray a muffin tray with cooking spray (avocado oil recommended). Add the batter to 12 muffin molds. Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 14-15 minutes.
Let the donuts rest for at least 15 minutes. They will continue to cook internally, so slightly underbaking is ideal.
Add the filling to a piping bag and cut a small hole in the center of each donut. Fill each donut with the prepared filling.
Add the frosting to the top of all the donuts. Then enjoy!

steps.instructionText: Simmer the blueberries, Splenda, honey, vanilla, and salt; stir in a cornstarch-and-water slurry and cook 4-6 min until thick and glossy. Cool 10-15 min.

Whisk the flour, oat flour, protein, oats, graham crumbs, baking powder, and salt. Cut in the cold butter to chunky crumbs, then fold in a mix of Greek yogurt, applesauce, egg, Splenda, and vanilla into a crumbly dough.
Press about 65% of the dough into a lined 8x8 pan; spread the filling; top with the remaining dough in clusters. Bake at 350F 34-38 min until golden and bubbling.
Cool fully, then chill 2 h before cutting into 9 bars.

notes.text: Keep the 27 g butter cold (straight from the fridge, cubed) and work quickly — if it warms and melts into the flour-protein mix you lose the chunky crumble texture and end up with a dense, uniform dough.

steps.instructionText: Mix the Greek yogurt, melted butter, and brown sugar. Stir in the flour, protein, baking powder, cinnamon, and nutmeg, then fold in the diced apple.

notes.text: 10–12 min at 350°F is tight for a protein-heavy batter with Greek yogurt — check at 10. The fritters should feel just set and spring back lightly; overcooked ones go rubbery as they cool.

steps.instructionText: Blend the protein, cottage cheese, Greek yogurt, vanilla pudding mix, Splenda, salt, and cinnamon until completely silky — the cottage cheese MUST blend out with no grain so it reads as mascarpone. Taste and adjust the Splenda (the cottage cheese and 0% yogurt are tangy, so the cream needs a real hit of sweetness), then let it rest about 10 minutes so the instant-pudding starch firms it to a thick, spoonable mascarpone-style cream.

Pour strong coffee into a shallow bowl. Dip each ladyfinger just about 1 second per side and roll it out — do NOT soak (oversoaked ladyfingers turn to mush, and they keep hydrating overnight). Line a dish, spread half the cream, and dust with cinnamon. Repeat with the remaining dipped ladyfingers and cream.

Dust the top with cocoa and refrigerate OVERNIGHT — at least 6 hours, ideally 24 — so the cream sets firm and the ladyfingers hydrate into cake. This set is what makes it tiramisu instead of pudding. Slice into 9 and serve cold.

notes.text: One second per side is the maximum dip — ladyfingers keep absorbing moisture overnight. Dip too long and by morning they're waterlogged mush, not soft cake. Use a timer if in doubt.

steps.instructionText: Blend the graham crackers to a fine crumb. Stir in the melted butter, protein powder, and salt until evenly combined, then gradually mix in the milk until the crumb just holds together (add more milk if it looks dry — it should press, not crumble).
Press firmly into a parchment-lined loaf pan. Freeze while you make the filling.
Blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, Splenda, protein, vanilla, lemon juice, salt, and pudding mix until completely smooth and creamy.
Spread the filling evenly over the frozen crust. Freeze at least 1.5 hr, or until firm.
Lift out by the parchment and slice into 12 bars. Eat straight from the freezer or after softening a few minutes.

notes.text: Press the crust very firmly — use the bottom of a measuring cup or a flat glass, working from center to edges. A loosely packed crust shatters when you slice the frozen bars.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a mixing bowl, add all wet ingredients and mix until smooth.
In another bowl, add all dry ingredients and mix.
Combine wet and dry ingredients.
Mix thoroughly until a thick batter forms, ensuring there are no clumps. Fold in mix-ins.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes to firm up the batter.
Prepare a parchment-lined cookie sheet or a baking sheet with cooking spray. Add batter.

Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes.
Remove when slightly underdone; they will continue to set as they cool. Cut into 88 blondies. Then enjoy!

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.
For the brownie layer: In a large bowl, whisk together pumpkin purée, Greek yogurt, egg, egg whites, almond milk, and vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together chocolate protein powder, cocoa powder, self-rising flour, sweetener, and salt.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spread the brownie batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
For the cheesecake filling: In a medium bowl, beat together cream cheese, Greek yogurt, protein powder, egg, sweetener, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Carefully spoon the cheesecake filling over the brownie batter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheesecake is set. Let cool completely.
For the stovetop caramel topping: In a small saucepan, combine sugar-free caramel syrup, almond milk, sweetener, cornstarch, and sea salt.
Whisk constantly over medium heat until the mixture thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
Pour the caramel topping over the cooled cheesecake layer and spread evenly.
Chill for at least 1 hour to set before cutting into bars.

slots.name: Torani sugar-free caramel syrup (or other brand)

notes.text: "Just combined" is critical here — this brownie layer has chocolate protein + cocoa + Greek yogurt + egg whites, all of which tighten fast when overmixed. Stop as soon as no dry flour streaks remain.

For the brownie layer: In a large bowl, whisk together pumpkin purée, Greek yogurt, egg, egg whites, almond milk, and vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together chocolate protein powder, cocoa powder, self-rising flour, sweetener, and salt.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spread the brownie batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
For the cheesecake filling: In a medium bowl, beat together cream cheese, Greek yogurt, protein powder, egg, sweetener, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Carefully spoon the cheesecake filling over the brownie batter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheesecake is set. Let cool completely.
For the stovetop caramel topping: In a small saucepan, combine sugar-free caramel syrup, almond milk, sweetener, cornstarch, and sea salt.
Whisk constantly over medium heat until the mixture thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
Pour the caramel topping over the cooled cheesecake layer and spread evenly.
Chill for at least 1 hour to set before cutting into bars.

slots.name: Torani sugar-free caramel syrup (or other brand)

notes.text: "Just combined" is critical here — this brownie layer has chocolate protein + cocoa + Greek yogurt + egg whites, all of which tighten fast when overmixed. Stop as soon as no dry flour streaks remain.
Bring the cream cheese and Greek yogurt to room temp before beating the cheesecake layer — cold dairy makes a lumpy filling that won't smooth out, and the lumps bake in permanently.
Don't beat air into the cheesecake layer — mix on low just until smooth. Airy cheesecake puffs in the oven, then cracks and sinks as it cools.

25–30 min is the window; pull when the cheesecake center has a slight wobble but isn't liquid — protein + Greek yogurt dry out fast past this point. The bars firm up fully only after cooling completely.

The Splenda-thickened caramel relies on cornstarch, not caramelization — if it's not thickening at 5 min, raise heat slightly and keep whisking. Stopping early leaves a watery sauce that soaks into the cheesecake.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a mixing bowl, combine the dry ingredients.
Add the wet ingredients to the dry ingredients and mix thoroughly. Place the batter in the fridge for 10 minutes to thicken.

Spray or line 2 small/medium circular baking dishes with parchment paper. Divide the batter evenly between the two dishes. Bake for 10-12 minutes, slightly underbaking. Let cool for at least 12 minutes.
While the cakes are cooling, prepare the filling frosting in another mixing bowl by stirring the ingredients together.
In a separate mixing bowl, prepare the top layer frosting by stirring the ingredients together.
Spread the mixed filling frosting onto one of the cooled cakes and place the other cake on top.
Apply the mixed top layer frosting to the top cake, then sprinkle with the topping ingredients. Chill in the refrigerator for at least 1 hour to allow the frosting to thicken before serving. Enjoy!

notes.text: 10–12 min is a ceiling, not a target — the casein + egg-white base dries out fast. Pull at 10 min when a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs; carryover heat in the pan finishes it during the 12-min rest.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.
Add the wet ingredients — egg, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla — and mix to a dough. If dry, add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.
Chill 20-30 min, then scoop onto a lined sheet, wet hands, and flatten (this dough barely spreads).
Bake at 350F for ~9 minutes — pull while the centers still look soft; they firm up as they cool.
Cool the cookies fully, then frost with the vanilla protein frosting (sub-recipe).

notes.text: 9 min is the target, not the floor — this dough has cornstarch, Greek yogurt, and 1.5 scoops of whey; another minute past "just set" edges produces a dry, cakey crumb instead of soft-centered.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180°C / 360°F.
In a large bowl, melt the peanut butter in the microwave until just melted.
Add the vanilla, water, sweetener drops, and the yoghurt. Mix well.
Add the baking powder, salt, protein powder, granulated sweetener, and coconut flour.
Mix until combined.
Pour the batter into a brownie tin or dish lined with baking paper.
Bake for 10 minutes. You want them to be just cooked so that they are still fudgey. Do not overcook them.
As soon as they come out of the oven, transfer them to a baking rack to cool so that they don’t continue cooking in the pan.

notes.text: 10 min is the hard ceiling — peanut butter + whey + coconut flour go from fudgy to dry-crumbly in the window between 10 and 13 min. Pull when the top looks just barely set and the center jiggles slightly.

steps.instructionText: Prepare the carrots by grating them.
In a large bowl, combine the grated carrots, nonfat Greek yogurt, egg, protein powder, banana, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and sweetener.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly until well combined.
Pour the batter into a prepared baking dish or individual ramekins.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a mixing bowl, add the wet ingredients and mix.
In another mixing bowl, add the dry ingredients and mix.
Combine the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly, avoiding clumps. Add the mix-in ingredients and mix again.
Chill the cookie dough in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Prepare a small/medium circular baking dish by lining it with parchment paper or spraying it with cooking spray. Add the cooled cookie dough to the baking dish.
If needed, wet your hands slightly and flatten the dough in the dish.
Bake at 350 degrees for 12-15 minutes. Remove from oven when slightly underdone, as it will continue to cook.
Let the cookie cake rest for 15 minutes. Optionally, decorate the sides of the cake with additional mini chocolate chips. Then enjoy!

notes.text: The Greek yogurt and cream cheese go in as wet ingredients — make sure both are at room temp or the cold dairy will clump against the butter and leave lumps that never smooth out.

payload.instructionText: Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, rolled oats, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. Add the splash of milk to bring it together so it holds its shape, not pours. Too stiff/dry -> a touch more milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Let it rest a few minutes so the oats hydrate, then taste for sweetness.

payload.text: Only 8 g of butter — it browns in under 2 min at medium heat. Watch from the moment it melts; the window between nutty and burnt is very short at this small quantity.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, rolled oats, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. Add the splash of milk to bring it together so it holds its shape, not pours. Too stiff/dry -> a touch more milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Let it rest a few minutes so the oats hydrate, then taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Only 8 g of butter — it browns in under 2 min at medium heat. Watch from the moment it melts; the window between nutty and burnt is very short at this small quantity.

Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, rolled oats, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. Add the splash of milk to bring it together so it holds its shape, not pours. Too stiff/dry -> a touch more milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Let it rest a few minutes so the oats hydrate, then taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Only 8 g of butter — it browns in under 2 min at medium heat. Watch from the moment it melts; the window between nutty and burnt is very short at this small quantity.
Let the dough rest 2-3 min after mixing before adjusting consistency: the oats and whey continue absorbing liquid, and what looks too wet will often firm to scoopable on its own.
9-11 min at 350F — pull while the centers still look underdone and pale. Whey protein bakes through on the hot tray; waiting for a set center means a dry, cakey cookie.
The 30-min chill is load-bearing with only 8 g butter: unchilled dough spreads flat before the edges set, killing the thick-center effect.
Don't judge texture off the tray — protein cookies are floppy when hot and feel underbaked. The full 10-15 min rest on the tray is when they firm to chewy.

Pull at a slight wobble in the center (~155-160F); a fully dry pick means it's already overcooked. This lean filling (cottage cheese + yogurt + whey) turns rubbery fast past done.
For the broiler method, freeze the assembled cheesecake 15-20 min first — the cold mass slows heat transfer so the 30 g brown sugar caramelizes to amber before the filling warms and weeps.
The brûlée shell softens within ~30 min on the cake; brûlée just before serving, not hours ahead, or it turns sticky and loses the crack.

1ca0442b-af33-4044-bc37-47fd935e8f9a.description: Creme brulee cheesecake on a graham crust: vanilla custard cheesecake over a par-baked graham crust, finished with a torched brown-sugar shell. A cheesecake is a baked custard, so the brulee crust is the signature; the graham base adds the classic restaurant form. The shell needs REAL sugar (sucralose will not caramelize) - ~30 g brown sugar in a thin even layer; everything else stays Splenda. Two finishes in the method: oven broiler (freeze first) or dry-pan caramel shards (no torch). About 183 cal/slice with the crust + bigger shell (was 140 crustless). To-make.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line a loaf tin. Whisk the egg, Greek yogurt, almond milk, melted butter, and lemon juice. Combine the flour, protein, Splenda, baking powder, and salt, then fold the dry into the wet. Fold in the blueberries and pour into the tin.

Stir the Splenda with the water into a glaze, spread over the cooled loaf, and chill 15 min to set. Slice into 8.

notes.text: 30-35 min is the ceiling — pull slightly underdone while the center still has a faint wobble. The Greek yogurt + protein batter keeps cooking as the loaf cools and goes rubbery fast if taken to a clean toothpick.

steps.instructionText: Mix flour, yogurt, and salt in a bowl until it clumps together.
Using floured hands, shape the dough into a boule. It should not be sticky. Add more flour if necessary.
Air fry at 175°C for 15-20 minutes using the air fry mode. Alternatively, oven bake at 175°C for 35 minutes. If the center is not cooked, flip the bread and cook for an additional 5 minutes.

notes.text: The dough should clump together immediately and feel like stiff playdough — if it's wet and shaggy the yogurt was too thin (brand matters). Add the extra flour before shaping, not after, or the surface gets uneven.

Using floured hands, shape the dough into a boule. It should not be sticky. Add more flour if necessary.
Air fry at 175°C for 15-20 minutes using the air fry mode. Alternatively, oven bake at 175°C for 35 minutes. If the center is not cooked, flip the bread and cook for an additional 5 minutes.

notes.text: The dough should clump together immediately and feel like stiff playdough — if it's wet and shaggy the yogurt was too thin (brand matters). Add the extra flour before shaping, not after, or the surface gets uneven.
Shape it into a tight boule before air frying: a loose, uneven mound will puff unevenly and the center stays raw while the outside firms. Tuck the seam underneath.
Air fry at 175C: don't go higher chasing speed — the crust sets and hardens before the center (only 120 g flour + 100 g yogurt) finishes cooking, leading to a gummy core.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 375F and line a sheet. Mix the eggs, applesauce, vanilla, and diced apple, then stir in the whey, oat flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and salt. Scoop into mounds with a cookie scoop.
Bake 12-15 min until golden. Cool slightly.
Whisk the whey, Splenda, milk, and vanilla into a glaze and drizzle over the warm bites.

notes.text: Toast the ground cinnamon in a dry pan 30–60 sec before adding it — straight from the jar it tastes flat; toasting blooms the oils and gives the fritter aroma you expect.

payload.instructionText: Chill only ~15 minutes (or let cold dough sit 10 min at room temp before baking). A fridge-cold center lags the most, so less chilling helps the middle keep pace.
Shape into 3 cookies and flatten into discs about 1/2 inch (1.5 cm) thick.
Bake at 325F / 160C on the middle rack for ~11-13 minutes. Pull when set but the centers still feel slightly soft.

payload.text: Let the browned butter cool 2–3 min before adding eggs — pour it in hot and you'll scramble the egg and break the emulsion, giving greasy cookies with a curdled look.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill only ~15 minutes (or let cold dough sit 10 min at room temp before baking). A fridge-cold center lags the most, so less chilling helps the middle keep pace.
Shape into 3 cookies and flatten into discs about 1/2 inch (1.5 cm) thick.
Bake at 325F / 160C on the middle rack for ~11-13 minutes. Pull when set but the centers still feel slightly soft.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Let the browned butter cool 2–3 min before adding eggs — pour it in hot and you'll scramble the egg and break the emulsion, giving greasy cookies with a curdled look.

65f81ebd-86bc-45e3-bc2b-1576d818b3b4.description: VERSION B - Even & Soft-Chewy: soft and chewy edge to edge, the same texture throughout with no raw-dough center. A pure-procedure variant of the gooey base - identical dough, ingredients, and macros; only the bake (steps 4-6) differs. Flattening the cookie and lowering the oven temp both shrink the edge-vs-center cook gap, so the whole cookie finishes together. Spreads a little more, no molten center.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F and line or grease an 8-inch cake pan.
Whisk eggs until light and frothy.
Mix in honey, Greek yogurt, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold in coconut, baking powder, and salt.
Pour batter into pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 28–35 minutes until golden and set in the center.

steps.instructionText: In a large bowl, combine the flour, vanilla protein powder, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt. Mix well.
Add the egg, melted light butter, Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, and almond milk to the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined and a dough forms. Be careful not to overmix.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Scoop the dough using an ice cream scooper and place onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oven when the tops still look slightly undercooked, as they will continue to set as they cool.

While the cookies are cooling, prepare the frosting by mixing the Greek yogurt, zero sugar Cool Whip, vanilla protein powder, sugar-free vanilla pudding mix, sweetener, and salt in a bowl until smooth and creamy. Place the frosting in the refrigerator.
For the cookie dough topping, combine the oat flour, vanilla protein powder, brown sugar, vanilla extract, and salt in a separate bowl.
Slowly add almond milk, a little at a time, until a cookie dough texture forms. Roll this mixture into 21 tiny balls.
Frost each cooled cookie with the prepared frosting.
Top each frosted cookie with the tiny cookie dough balls and chocolate chips. Enjoy!

notes.text: Pull at 8–9 min when tops look slightly underdone — the Greek yogurt + protein base sets firm on cooling. 10 min is the hard ceiling; a fully dry-looking top at the oven means rubbery cookies by the time they're frosted.

notes.text: Pull at 8–9 min when tops look slightly underdone — the Greek yogurt + protein base sets firm on cooling. 10 min is the hard ceiling; a fully dry-looking top at the oven means rubbery cookies by the time they're frosted.

a38f0052-f417-4efe-8137-8ea6bb2fc145.name: Toasted Coconut Protein Cheesecake
a38f0052-f417-4efe-8137-8ea6bb2fc145.author: system

payload.instructionText: Toast 65 g shredded coconut in a dry skillet over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until golden and fragrant (it colors fast then burns - watch it). Cool. Grind 45 g to a fine meal (spice grinder or food processor) and beat it into the filling with the wet ingredients in step 3 so the coconut disperses throughout; reserve the other 20 g for the topping.
Once the cheesecake is fully chilled, scatter the reserved 20 g toasted coconut evenly over the top just before serving (keeps it crisp).

payload.text: Shredded coconut goes from golden to burnt in under a minute — use medium heat and stir constantly; pull the skillet off the heat the moment it smells fragrant, as residual pan heat will darken it another shade.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

payload.instructionText: Caramelize the banana: slice and cook in a nonstick pan over medium heat with a sprinkle of sweetener until golden, ~2-3 min per side. Add the pumpkin to the same pan and cook 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. In the last ~45-60 sec, stir the ground cinnamon into the hot fruit to toast it — it should turn fragrant and deepen a shade. Toast it in the fruit, not in a dry pan: loose ground cinnamon scorches in seconds, but the fruit's moisture buffers it so it blooms evenly. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).

Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles. For the topping, toast the graham crumbs with the garnish cinnamon in a dry pan over medium heat ~1 min, stirring, until fragrant, then let cool. Scatter over the cheesecake after baking so they stay crisp.
Finish with sugar-free cinnamon syrup to taste.

payload.text: The cooled fruit is non-negotiable — even slightly warm banana/pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs the moment they meet in s4, giving you scrambled curds in the batter.

da613343-8cad-4525-ac28-cd3826e29885.name: Caramelized Biscuit Chocolate Banana Protein Cake
da613343-8cad-4525-ac28-cd3826e29885.description: A high protein, high fibre, flourless, no added sugar, probiotic, simple, macro-friendly cake layered with caramelised biscuit protein cream and a low-calorie biscoff and choc sauce. Perfect for satisfying chocolate cravings while staying on track with fitness goals. House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. Imported via `batch ingest`.
da613343-8cad-4525-ac28-cd3826e29885.author: system

steps.instructionText: In a bowl, whisk your egg, then add mashed banana, cacao, and optional sweetener to taste. Mix until combined. Alternatively, add all ingredients to a blender and mix until smooth.
Pour into a greased large ramekin (12cm) and microwave for 3 minutes on high (900w) or until a toothpick test comes out clean.
Cool the cake, then slice horizontally to create two layers.
For the filling: in a bowl, mix your yogurt with vegan protein until combined and spreadable. Add some water if it’s too thick. Spread half of the filling evenly on the bottom layer.
Place the top layer back onto the filled bottom layer.
Spread the remainder of the filling on top.
Garnish: mix biscoff spread with water until you get a sauce consistency and drizzle over the cake. Optionally, add some no-added-sugar choc sauce or cacao sauce for extra deliciousness.

notes.text: Microwaves vary — 3 min at 900w is the spec, but check at 2 min 15 sec. A protein-banana mug cake goes from done to rubbery in under 30 seconds of overshoot; pull when a toothpick has a few moist crumbs, not bone-dry.

ef1267a2-45b6-4670-a169-012f2742510c.description: Frozen yogurt mold bars: nonfat Greek yogurt whipped with chocolate protein and butterscotch SF pudding mix, folded with crushed Ghost cinnamon cereal, set in candy-bar molds, topped with more cereal and a drizzle of zero-sugar chocolate syrup. steps.instructionText: Whisk the Greek yogurt, milk, butterscotch pudding mix, and chocolate protein until smooth. Crush about half the cereal and fold it in.
Pour into candy-bar molds. Sprinkle the remaining cereal on top and drizzle with the zero-sugar chocolate syrup.
Freeze 6-12 hr until firm, then unmold. Makes 6 bars.

notes.text: The butterscotch SF pudding mix and 2 scoops of chocolate protein thicken fast once whisked — the 15 g of skim milk is the working liquid; don't over-add or the bars won't set firm enough to unmold cleanly.

steps.instructionText: In a bowl, use a hand blender or whisk to mix the cake ingredients until smooth.
Add the baking powder and a splash of water, then gently fold to combine.
Pour the batter into a greased ramekin and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 20 minutes.
Let cool slightly, then top with yoghurt, chopped nuts, cinnamon, and maple syrup.

notes.text: 180C for 20 min is for a full-size ramekin — check at 15 min by pressing the center lightly. With only 30 g vegan protein as the flour-stand-in, this single-serve cake overbakes quickly and turns chalky-dry.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.
Add the wet ingredients — egg, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla — and mix to a dough. If dry, add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.
Chill 20-30 min, then scoop onto a lined sheet, wet hands, and flatten (this dough barely spreads).
Bake at 350F for ~9 minutes — pull while the centers still look soft; they firm up as they cool.
Cool the cookies fully. Whisk the drizzle (lemon juice + Splenda) smooth and spoon over the cookies.

0b9efee2-d0ff-4091-b7ce-0991dc8d0475.description: Healthy protein ice cream sandwiches in the style of Fat Boys: a blended vanilla protein 'ice cream' between chocolate graham crackers. Source: healthbeet.org. Decent as-is; the filling really wants a Ninja Creami churn for texture. Stated macros ~135 kcal / 16C / 13-14P / 3F per sandwich.
0b9efee2-d0ff-4091-b7ce-0991dc8d0475.author: user

steps.instructionText: Blend the protein powder, almond milk, pudding mix, Greek yogurt, vanilla, and salt smooth in a blender.
Freeze ~6 hours, until mostly frozen. Re-churn in a Ninja Creami (best) or re-blend in a food processor.
Line a cake pan with parchment and arrange half-sheets of graham cracker, 6 across the bottom.
Spread the ice cream over the crackers until all are covered.
Top with a second graham cracker and return to the freezer until frozen. Slice into 6 sandwiches.

notes.text: If you have a Ninja Creami: freeze 24 hr (not 6) for the best churn — the full freeze gives a denser base that re-processes into a creamier texture; the 6-hr option works but comes out icier.

payload.instructionText: Pour half the filling onto the cooled crust. Drop spoonfuls of the protein caramel swirl over it, add the rest of the filling, then drag a knife through in a few S-strokes to marble (don't overmix). Tap the pan on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Once fully chilled (ideally overnight), lift the cake out with the parchment sling onto a plate. Warm the caramel and the ganache separately just until pourable — a few seconds; they should ribbon, not run. Drizzle both over the top in a back-and-forth criss-cross (use a spoon, or a zip-top bag with a tiny corner snipped). Finish with a pinch of flaky salt. Slice with a hot, wiped knife.

payload.text: Mix on low after adding eggs — the 2.5 scoops of vanilla protein make this batter dense and prone to aeration. Overbeating here traps air that expands in the oven, then collapses and cracks the top.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).

Pour half the filling onto the cooled crust. Drop spoonfuls of the protein caramel swirl over it, add the rest of the filling, then drag a knife through in a few S-strokes to marble (don't overmix). Tap the pan on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

Once fully chilled (ideally overnight), lift the cake out with the parchment sling onto a plate. steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line a baking sheet. Whisk the protein, oat flour, coconut flour, baking powder, and salt. Add the Greek yogurt, maple syrup, egg, and vanilla; mix to a thick cookie dough. Fold in the sprinkles.
Divide into 4 large cookies and gently flatten the tops. Bake 10-12 min until the edges are set. Cool completely before frosting.
Mix the Greek yogurt, protein, pudding mix, and vanilla until smooth and creamy. Frost the cooled cookies and top with extra sprinkles.

notes.text: Coconut flour is highly absorbent — it will keep thickening the dough as it sits. If the dough feels workable right after mixing, don't add milk yet; give it 2 minutes before deciding.

8c2fb412-b57e-44d4-9c88-c2e1b00431c3.name: Fudgy + Chewy Protein Brownies
8c2fb412-b57e-44d4-9c88-c2e1b00431c3.author: user

payload.instructionText: Melt the butter + baking chocolate (low heat or short microwave bursts). Stir in the cocoa + espresso to bloom into a paste; set aside to cool slightly.

Beat the whole egg + egg white with the brown sugar only until the sugar grit dissolves and it looks smooth and glossy — then STOP. This builds chew and the shiny top; do NOT whip it to a pale, voluminous ribbon, which aerates it and bakes up holey/cakey.
Stir the Greek yogurt into the egg mixture, then fold in the cooled chocolate mixture until uniform.
Whisk the flour + protein powder + salt, then fold in just to no dry streaks — then a few extra gentle strokes for a little chew, stopping before the batter turns smooth and stretchy. No cornstarch.
Stir in the Splenda; add a splash of skim milk only if the batter is stiff. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~17–18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at a slight center jiggle — it's fudgy-leaning, so on the early side.

payload.text: Let the melted butter + chocolate cool until just warm before adding to the eggs — pouring hot chocolate into the egg mixture scrambles it and you lose the glossy emulsion the shiny top depends on.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 325°F (165°C) and line or grease a small ~6-inch square pan.
Melt the butter + baking chocolate (low heat or short microwave bursts). Stir in the cocoa + espresso to bloom into a paste; set aside to cool slightly.

Beat the whole egg + egg white with the brown sugar only until the sugar grit dissolves and it looks smooth and glossy — then STOP. This builds chew and the shiny top; do NOT whip it to a pale, voluminous ribbon, which aerates it and bakes up holey/cakey.
Stir the Greek yogurt into the egg mixture, then fold in the cooled chocolate mixture until uniform.
Whisk the flour + protein powder + salt, then fold in just to no dry streaks — then a few extra gentle strokes for a little chew, stopping before the batter turns smooth and stretchy. No cornstarch.
Stir in the Splenda; add a splash of skim milk only if the batter is stiff. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~17–18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at a slight center jiggle — it's fudgy-leaning, so on the early side.

Doneness: edges set and just pulling from the sides with a slight wobble in the center (not a liquid slosh). A toothpick should read moist crumbs clinging — a clean toothpick means overbaked. On these small protein batters, trust the jiggle over the toothpick.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, undisturbed — never cut warm. The crumb sets and the protein firms as it cools; a warm one seems gummy and then comes good.

Chill a few hours or overnight — they're better the next day. Cut cold with a clean knife (for the fudgy ones, run it under hot water and wipe between cuts). Store airtight; freeze portions for longer keeping. Optional: microwave a piece 8–10 sec to soften the fat — no longer, or the protein turns rubbery.

notes.text: Let the melted butter + chocolate cool until just warm before adding to the eggs — pouring hot chocolate into the egg mixture scrambles it and you lose the glossy emulsion the shiny top depends on.

8c2fb412-b57e-44d4-9c88-c2e1b00431c3.description: The balanced one — derived from the Fudgy base, keeping real fudge from butter + baking chocolate but adding chew: the whole egg + an extra egg white are beaten with brown sugar until glossy (dissolved, never whipped to a ribbon), the cornstarch is dropped, and protein is doubled. 1/4 cup granulated Splenda, no added milk, baked at 325F for ~17-18 min and pulled at a slight (fudgy-leaning) jiggle. Doubling protein at flat calories pulls the ratio from the base's 16.6 down to 12.5 cal per g protein. Computed ~614 cal / 49 g protein per batch of 9; ~68 cal, 5.5P, 6.7C, 2.7F per square. Medium eggs (44 g whole, 30 g white). Source: user.

steps.instructionText: In separate bowls, mix the wet ingredients and the dry ingredients.
Combine the wet and dry mixtures together.
Fill a springform pan no more than halfway up. The pan size can be 5, 6, or 7 inches.
Bake at 305°F for 15 minutes. The baking temperature is lower because the oven runs hot. After 15 minutes, cover the cake with aluminum foil and bake for another 8 minutes.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan for at least 15 minutes without disturbing it.
While the cake is cooling, prepare the frosting by mixing the frosting ingredients until the mixture is thick.
Spread the frosting over the cooled cake.
Enjoy your cake!

Chef’s Note: To make removal easier, line your springform pan with cooking spray and parchment paper. Cut parchment paper to fit the bottom, spray the bottom to help it stick, and then spray the sides.

4398e923-4bc4-4fcb-a329-c5c7eb5aa105.author: user

steps.instructionText: Mix everything together to form the dough.
Bake at 350°F for 7-8 minutes.

notes.text: Coconut flour absorbs moisture aggressively and walnuts add bulk — the dough will stiffen within 2 minutes of mixing. Don't judge spreadability immediately; let it rest a moment, then portion.

Mix nut butter (walnuts here are the structural binder) and egg together first until fully emulsified before adding the dry ingredients — this prevents dry pockets of protein powder in the finished cookie.

7–8 min at 350°F is the ceiling for 6 cookies this size — pull when edges are just set and centres still look slightly underdone. The Kinder chocolate holds residual heat and the protein finishes cooking on the pan.

Press the Kinder slices gently into the tops right before baking rather than mixing them into the dough — they stay whole, melt slightly into the surface, and look clean rather than disappearing into the cookie.

steps.instructionText: Blend the pumpkin, applesauce, Splenda, egg whites, vanilla, cocoa, oats, protein, and baking soda into a smooth batter. Divide between 2-3 parchment-lined pans.
Bake at 350F for 20-40 min (toothpick clean), depending on pan depth. Cool 10 min in the pan, then turn out and cool completely.
Mix the Laughing Cow, Greek yogurt, Splenda, vanilla, and vanilla protein smooth.
Mix the Laughing Cow, Greek yogurt, Splenda, cocoa, and chocolate protein smooth.
Coat the first layer with the vanilla icing, stack the second and coat with the chocolate icing, then top with the final layer. Refrigerate ~30 min before cutting into 4.

notes.text: The 20–40 min window is huge because pan depth varies — in 2 thin layers a single layer can be done in 18–22 min while a deep 2-layer pan takes 35+. Start checking at 18 min and go by toothpick, not time.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.
Add the wet ingredients — egg, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla — and mix to a dough. If dry, add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.
Chill 20-30 min, then scoop onto a lined sheet, wet hands, and flatten (this dough barely spreads).
Bake at 350F for ~9 minutes — pull while the centers still look soft; they firm up as they cool.
Cool the cookies fully, then frost with the vanilla protein frosting (sub-recipe).

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line an 8x8 dish. Whisk the cottage cheese, eggs, vanilla, and SF maple syrup, then mix in the flour, grated carrot, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt. Spread into the dish.
Bake 25-30 min. Cool completely.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the Splenda into an icing, spread over the cooled bars, and dust with cinnamon. Cut into 9.

notes.text: The 25–30 min window is wide; cottage-cheese batters in an 8x8 can set as early as 22 min. Pull when the edges are set and a pick reads moist crumbs — a clean pick means they're already over.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line an 8x8 dish. Whisk the cottage cheese, eggs, vanilla, and SF maple syrup, then mix in the flour, grated carrot, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt. Spread into the dish.
Bake 25-30 min. Cool completely.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the Splenda into an icing, spread over the cooled bars, and dust with cinnamon. Cut into 9.

notes.text: The 25–30 min window is wide; cottage-cheese batters in an 8x8 can set as early as 22 min. Pull when the edges are set and a pick reads moist crumbs — a clean pick means they're already over.
Blend the cottage cheese smooth before mixing — unblended curds leave wet pockets that never fully bake through, and the texture reads lumpy even after cutting.
Don't cut warm — cottage-cheese bars are gummy and tear until fully cooled. Cool completely on a rack before refrigerating, then cut cold for clean squares.
Grate the carrot fine (box-grater small holes) at 55 g; coarse shreds stay chewy and release water pockets mid-bake. Pat dry after grating if they feel very wet.

The Splenda icing is thin when first mixed; spread it right before serving or it pools around the sides. If you want it to hold shape as a layer, stir in an extra tsp of Splenda and chill 10 min first.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 325°F (165°C) and line or grease a small ~6-inch square pan.
Melt the butter + baking chocolate over low heat or in short microwave bursts. Stir in the cocoa + espresso powder to bloom them in the warm fat — it becomes a thick paste.

Stir in the skim milk to loosen and finish blooming; warm gently to combine. For chunky brownies, reserve 1–2 tsp of the thick paste, stir a pinch of Splenda into it, and set aside. Off the heat, cool to just warm.
Stir in the Splenda, then the Greek yogurt and vanilla.
Lightly beat the egg (no whipping — keep air out so it bakes fudgy, not cakey) and stir in last. If the base is still warm, temper first: stir a spoonful of base into the egg, then add it back.

Whisk the flour + cornstarch + protein powder + salt, then fold into the batter by hand just until no dry streaks remain — then stop. A few small lumps are fine; mixing past this develops gluten and bakes up cakey. Smooth finish: fold uniform. Chunky finish: fold in the reserved sweetened paste at the very end so it stays in pockets. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at a slight center jiggle (not a liquid slosh) — it should look a touch underdone; carryover heat and cooling finish the set.

Doneness: edges set and just pulling from the sides with a slight wobble in the center (not a liquid slosh). A toothpick should read moist crumbs clinging — a clean toothpick means overbaked. On these small protein batters, trust the jiggle over the toothpick.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, undisturbed — never cut warm. The crumb sets and the protein firms as it cools; a warm one seems gummy and then comes good.

Chill a few hours or overnight — they're better the next day. Cut cold with a clean knife (for the fudgy ones, run it under hot water and wipe between cuts). Store airtight; freeze portions for longer keeping. Optional: microwave a piece 8–10 sec to soften the fat — no longer, or the protein turns rubbery.

notes.text: Don't whip the egg — just break the yolk and stir it in gently. Beating in air makes the batter puff in the oven and bake cakey; keeping it still keeps it dense and fudgy.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F and line an 8x8 inch pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together the greek yogurt, almond milk, apple sauce, egg, oil, and vanilla.
Add the protein pancake mix and protein powder to the wet ingredients and mix until just combined.
Set the cake batter aside.
For the streusel, add all streusel ingredients in a bowl and use your hands to combine until you get a sugary crumble.
Pour half of the cake batter into the prepared pan and layer half of the streusel crumble over the top.
Pour the remaining batter over the streusel and sprinkle the remaining streusel mix on top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean but the cake should still be moist.
Let the coffee cake cool completely on a baking rack.
Mix the icing ingredients together and drizzle over the top of the cooled coffee cake.
Slice and enjoy!

notes.text: A clean toothpick here means overbaked — this protein + Greek yogurt batter dries out quickly. Pull at 30 min when a pick comes out with a few moist crumbs; the cake firms as it cools.

steps.instructionText: Mix all the cake ingredients together.
Pour the batter evenly into lined 6-inch cake tins.
Bake at 350°F for 20-25 minutes. Do not overbake! Keep an eye on it and use a toothpick to check for doneness.
Allow the cake to cool completely before mixing the frosting and assembling. It is usually best to wait a whole day before decorating and putting it all together.
Enjoy your delicious low-calorie, high-protein coconut cake!

notes.text: 20–25 min at 350°F is tight for a whey + applesauce batter — start checking at 18 min. Pull when a toothpick reads a few moist crumbs; a clean pick means the crumb is already drying out.
Bring the Greek yogurt (both the cake and frosting portions) to room temp before mixing — cold yogurt clumps around the protein powder and leaves dry lumps that don't bake out.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Crush graham crackers and mix with maple syrup. Press this mixture onto the bottom of a 9x5 loaf pan.
Combine all brownie ingredients in a bowl and mix well. Spread this batter evenly over the graham cracker base.
Bake for approximately 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Be careful not to overbake, as this can affect the fudgy texture.
While the brownies bake, prepare the frosting by mixing all frosting ingredients together until smooth. If using pudding mix, add it to thicken the frosting.
Once the brownies have cooled slightly, spread the frosting evenly over the top.

Sprinkle crushed graham crackers over the frosting. If desired, prepare the chocolate drizzle by melting the oil and chocolate together in the microwave in 30-second intervals until smooth, then drizzle over the brownies.
Cut the brownies into four pieces to create squares. For the best texture and flavor, chill the brownies in the refrigerator before serving.

notes.text: 45 min is dangerously long for a Greek yogurt + pumpkin batter — check at 30 min. Pull when a pick reads moist crumbs; the pumpkin holds moisture but the protein still turns rubbery if pushed past set.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 180°C and grease a mini cake tin (4 inch).
Sieve all dry ingredients for the cake into a mixing bowl and whisk to combine.
Add wet ingredients for the cake into a separate bowl and mix to combine.
Pour the cake batter into the mini cake tin and bake for 20 minutes, or until cooked through. Remove from oven and let it cool.
While the cake is cooling, prepare the frosting by adding all frosting ingredients to a bowl and stirring to combine. Chill in the fridge for 10-15 minutes to thicken.
Once the cake has cooled and the frosting has thickened, cut the cake in half and spread Biscoff frosting between the layers.
Place the top half of the cake on and coat the entire cake with the remaining frosting.
Enjoy your creation!

notes.text: 20 min at 180°C (356°F) is exact for a 4-inch mini cake; don't judge by color — whey protein browns before it's done. Use a toothpick and pull at moist crumbs; the small mass overbakes in under 2 extra minutes.

steps.instructionText: Simmer the blueberries, Splenda, honey, vanilla, and salt; stir in a cornstarch-and-water slurry and cook 4-6 min until thick and glossy. Cool 10-15 min.

Whisk the flour, oat flour, protein, oats, graham crumbs, baking powder, and salt. Cut in the cold butter to chunky crumbs, then fold in a mix of Greek yogurt, applesauce, egg, Splenda, and vanilla into a crumbly dough.
Press about 65% of the dough into a lined 8x8 pan; spread the filling; top with the remaining dough in clusters. Bake at 350F 34-38 min until golden and bubbling.
Cool fully, then chill 2 h before cutting into 9 bars.

notes.text: Keep the 27 g butter cold (straight from the fridge, cubed) and work quickly — if it warms and melts into the flour-protein mix you lose the chunky crumble texture and end up with a dense, uniform dough.

Mix the cornstarch slurry into the simmering blueberries off-heat or at a low bubble — high heat scorches it immediately. The filling should coat a spoon thickly before you take it off; it firms further as it cools.
34–38 min is the window; pull at 34 and check the crumble top for golden color. The protein powder in the crumble means the dough beneath will dry out and turn chalky if baked past set.
Press the base layer firmly and evenly — a light press leaves gaps that cause the filling to sink through when it bakes. Use the bottom of a measuring cup to compact it.
The full 2-hour chill is non-negotiable for clean cuts: the cornstarch-set blueberry filling and the soft protein crumb both tear and smear when warm. Slice with a sharp knife wiped between cuts.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and grease an 8x8 dish. Mix the Greek yogurt, protein, eggs, applesauce, Splenda, and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the oat flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and baking soda, then fold in the shredded carrot and walnuts. Spread into the dish.
Bake 25-30 min until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Whip the cream cheese, Greek yogurt, protein, Splenda, and vanilla until smooth and spread over the cooled cake. Cut into 9.

notes.text: 25 min is the floor, not the target — the 110g of carrot adds moisture and a lean oat-flour batter can look underdone at 25 min but carry-over finishes it. Pull when a toothpick comes clean and the edges pull slightly from the pan.
Grate the carrots fine, not coarse — coarse shreds don't hydrate fully in the short bake and leave wet pockets that make the center sink.
Cool completely before frosting — this cake is thin (8x8) and stays warm longer than it looks. Frosting a warm square melts the cream cheese-yogurt mix into a wet glaze.
The light cream cheese must be at room temp before beating — cold cream cheese stays lumpy even with yogurt and protein stirred in, and the frosting won't smooth out.
If the frosting is too loose to hold shape, chill it 20 min before spreading — the cold firms the cream cheese and lets the protein powder fully hydrate, giving a clean spreadable texture.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F and line or grease an 8-inch cake pan.
Whisk eggs until light and frothy.
Mix in honey, Greek yogurt, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold in coconut, baking powder, and salt.
Pour batter into pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 28–35 minutes until golden and set in the center.
Cool for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes.text: 28 min is the floor; pull at the first sign of a set center with only a faint wobble and a golden top — the 3-egg + Greek yogurt base continues cooking as it cools, and a fully dry center at 35 min will be rubbery when sliced.

Whisk the eggs until genuinely light and frothy — 1–2 min by hand — before adding anything else; in a flourless cake the egg aeration is the main structural lift (the bit of baking powder only assists), and skipping it gives a dense, flat result.
Use room-temperature Greek yogurt; cold yogurt mixed into warm frothy eggs deflates the air you just built and can leave cold pockets that bake unevenly.
Fold the coconut in gently — it absorbs moisture during the bake, so overmixing at this stage tightens the batter and can make the cake gummy rather than tender.
The full 10-min rest in the pan is mandatory — this cake has no flour skeleton; slicing while warm tears it. Cool on a rack and run a knife around the edge before unmolding.

steps.instructionText: Combine the whey isolate, collagen, cocoa, and salt. Separately whisk the melted butter, honey, vanilla, and water, then stir into the dry until a thick dough forms. Press firmly into a parchment-lined loaf pan.
Melt the coconut oil, cocoa, and honey together until smooth and spread over the bars.
Refrigerate until firm, then slice into 10 bars.

notes.text: Honey (100 g in the dough) is the structural binder — don't thin the dough with extra water beyond the 2 tsp written. A wetter dough won't set firm enough to slice cleanly after refrigeration.
Press the dough firmly into the loaf pan in an even layer — air pockets make bars crumble when sliced. Use the back of a spoon or wet fingers to pack it tight before adding the shell.

Chill the pressed dough until firm before spreading the coconut-oil shell — if you spread it over still-soft, freshly pressed dough the shell soaks in instead of setting as a distinct layer. A 10–15 min stint in the fridge or freezer firms it up first.
Let refrigerated bars temper 3–5 min at room temperature before eating — straight from the fridge the coconut-oil shell is rock-hard and snaps aggressively.
Whey isolate (100 g) and collagen (80 g) both clump when added to liquid — whisk dry ingredients together first so cocoa is evenly distributed before the butter-honey mixture goes in.

steps.instructionText: Stir the cocoa, protein, espresso powder, oat flour, and salt together. Add the maple syrup, pumpkin, vanilla, and most of the milk and mix to a thick fudgy dough — add the rest of the milk a little at a time only if needed (a little goes a long way). Fold in the chocolate chips and melted butter.
Press the dough firmly into a parchment-lined loaf pan. Freeze 10 min (or refrigerate ~1 hr) until set, then slice into 8 bars. Store in the fridge.

notes.text: Add the 75 g milk gradually — with 3 scoops protein + 42 g oat flour, the dough tightens fast and a little milk goes a long way. Overshoot and the bars won't hold their shape after freezing.

The 2.5 tbsp maple syrup is the structural binder, not just sweetener — don't reduce it or swap for a dry sweetener. If you need less sweetness, cut the syrup by at most 1 tsp and compensate with a splash of milk.
Press the dough very firmly into the loaf pan — use the back of a flat spatula or a piece of parchment on top and press down hard. Loose pressing leaves crumbly bars that fall apart when sliced.
After 10 min in the freezer the bars are rock-solid; let them temper at room temperature for 3–5 minutes before biting, or the frozen butter and chocolate-chip fat make them tooth-crackingly hard.
The 60 g pumpkin puree adds moisture and binding without flavor — use plain canned pumpkin, not pumpkin pie filling, which has spices and added sugar that will throw off the balance.

steps.instructionText: Mix all the cake ingredients together.
Pour the batter evenly into lined 6-inch cake tins.
Bake at 350°F for 20-25 minutes. Do not overbake! Keep an eye on it and use a toothpick to check for doneness.
Allow the cake to cool completely before mixing the frosting and assembling. It is usually best to wait a whole day before decorating and putting it all together.
Enjoy your delicious low-calorie, high-protein coconut cake!

notes.text: 20–25 min at 350°F is tight for a whey + applesauce batter — start checking at 18 min. Pull when a toothpick reads a few moist crumbs; a clean pick means the crumb is already drying out.
Bring the Greek yogurt (both the cake and frosting portions) to room temp before mixing — cold yogurt clumps around the protein powder and leaves dry lumps that don't bake out.

The frosting is Greek yogurt + light cream cheese — it will weep and slide off a warm cake. Wait until the cake is fully cooled (or even chilled overnight) before assembling; the step's advice here is worth following.

The baking soda (1 tsp) is a strong leavener for a thin 6-inch tin — don't add more thinking it'll help rise. Too much makes the center dome and crack aggressively, and the alkalinity dulls the coconut flavor.
Make the frosting first and chill it 10–15 min before spreading. The cold cream cheese is what firms it up, so it pipes and spreads cleanly once set rather than weeping off the cake.

steps.instructionText: In a bowl, use a hand blender or whisk to mix the cake ingredients until smooth.
Add the baking powder and a splash of water, then gently fold to combine.
Pour the batter into a greased ramekin and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 20 minutes.
Let cool slightly, then top with yoghurt, chopped nuts, cinnamon, and maple syrup.

notes.text: 180C for 20 min is for a full-size ramekin — check at 15 min by pressing the center lightly. With only 30 g vegan protein as the flour-stand-in, this single-serve cake overbakes quickly and turns chalky-dry.
Grate the 30 g carrot on the fine side of the grater, not coarse — fine shreds blend into the batter and soften fully in 20 min, while coarse shreds can stay crunchy in such a short bake.
Add the baking powder with the splash of water, not dry into the dry batter — in a batter this small, a dry pocket of baking powder can create a bitter spot and uneven rise.
Let the cake cool at least 5 min before topping with the 50 g Greek yogurt — warm cake makes the yogurt immediately runny and it slides off; a brief rest firms the surface enough to hold it.

steps.instructionText: In separate bowls, mix the wet ingredients and the dry ingredients.
Combine the wet and dry mixtures together.
Fill a springform pan no more than halfway up. The pan size can be 5, 6, or 7 inches.
Bake at 305°F for 15 minutes. The baking temperature is lower because the oven runs hot. After 15 minutes, cover the cake with aluminum foil and bake for another 8 minutes.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan for at least 15 minutes without disturbing it.
While the cake is cooling, prepare the frosting by mixing the frosting ingredients until the mixture is thick.
Spread the frosting over the cooled cake.
Enjoy your cake!

Chef’s Note: To make removal easier, line your springform pan with cooking spray and parchment paper. Cut parchment paper to fit the bottom, spray the bottom to help it stick, and then spray the sides.

notes.text: Cream the 113 g butter with the Splenda and honey first until pale, then add eggs one at a time — this builds structure so the Greek yogurt and protein fold in without deflating or curdling the batter.
With 2 scoops of whey in the batter, overmixing after combining wet and dry produces a rubbery, dense crumb. Fold until just no dry streaks remain and stop immediately.

305°F is deliberately low — don't bump the temperature. At a normal 350°F the protein sets the outside fast while the 3-egg interior stays wet, then cracks. The foil tent at 15 min prevents the top from over-browning during the final 8 minutes.
Don't skip the 15-minute in-pan rest — this cake is fragile warm and will tear if released from the springform too soon. Let it cool in the pan undisturbed before running the ring.

The Greek yogurt frosting is thickened by the casein (sl3) — it will firm up as it sits. Mix it just before frosting; if it thickens too much to spread, a tiny splash of milk loosens it without breaking it.

payload.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl - flour, cocoa, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.

Add the wet ingredients - egg, egg white, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla, the red gel coloring, and the vinegar - and mix to a dough. Cocoa makes this drier, so add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.
Cool the cookies fully, then frost with the protein cream-cheese frosting (sub-recipe).

payload.text: 3 tbsp cocoa makes this dough noticeably drier than the plain Crumbl base — don't judge hydration by how the plain version felt. Add almond milk slowly, 1 tsp at a time, until the dough just coheres; over-wetting leads to flat, spreading cookies.
Use gel food coloring, not liquid — the 1 tsp of liquid coloring adds measurable moisture and will shift the dough hydration; gel gives vivid color with a few drops and doesn't thin the batter.

Pull at 9 min with soft centers — cocoa masks the visual cues (the cookies look set and darker earlier than they are). Test by pressing the edge; it should be firm while the center still gives slightly.
The cream-cheese frosting needs to be fully chilled and the cookies fully cool before piping — warm cookies and a soft frosting will merge into a smeared glaze rather than a clean dollop.
The 1 tsp ACV in the cookie is for tang, not lift — leavening is baking powder only. Don't increase the vinegar; more acid will interfere with the baking powder and make the cookies flat.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Whisk wet ingredients until smooth.
Add dry ingredients and mix into a thick, slightly glossy batter.
Fold in chips and chunks.
Transfer the batter to a greased 5–6 inch springform pan or skillet.
Top with optional toppings.
Bake for 15-20 minutes. Pull when the center is slightly underdone for a gooey, oozing center and to prevent it from drying out.

notes.text: Pull at 15 minutes and check — casein protein thickens as it bakes and the applesauce holds moisture early, then the center goes rubbery fast if it crosses done. A slightly glossy, jiggly center is correct; a matte, firm center is already overbaked.

The batter uses casein (not whey) — casein is thicker and slower to hydrate. Let the mixed batter rest 2–3 minutes before transferring to the pan; it will thicken to the right consistency without adding flour.
A 5–6 inch springform or cast-iron skillet is correct; a larger pan spreads the batter too thin and it bakes through before the center sets gooey. Don't use a standard 8-inch cake pan.
The SF maple syrup (40 ml) is structural moisture here — don't substitute with Splenda dry sweetener, which would remove liquid and make the batter stiff and cakey.

steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 180°C / 360°F.
In a large bowl, melt the peanut butter in the microwave until just melted.
Add the vanilla, water, sweetener drops, and the yoghurt. Mix well.
Add the baking powder, salt, protein powder, granulated sweetener, and coconut flour.
Mix until combined.
Pour the batter into a brownie tin or dish lined with baking paper.
Bake for 10 minutes. You want them to be just cooked so that they are still fudgey. Do not overcook them.
As soon as they come out of the oven, transfer them to a baking rack to cool so that they don’t continue cooking in the pan.

notes.text: 10 min is the hard ceiling — peanut butter + whey + coconut flour go from fudgy to dry-crumbly in the window between 10 and 13 min. Pull when the top looks just barely set and the center jiggles slightly.
Transfer to a rack immediately — leaving the blondies in the hot tin keeps cooking them and kills the fudgy texture the recipe depends on.
Melt peanut butter until just fluid, not hot — if it's too hot when you add the Greek yogurt, the yogurt seizes and separates, making the batter grainy.

Coconut flour (28 g) absorbs liquid aggressively — don't add extra water to loosen the batter. If it looks thick, that's correct; a runny batter means over-hydrated coconut flour and a gummy, dense bar.
Cool fully before cutting — warm protein blondies are gummy and tear. At least 20 min on the rack gives a clean slice and the fudgy set the recipe promises.

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line a loaf tin. Whisk the egg, Greek yogurt, almond milk, melted butter, and lemon juice. Combine the flour, protein, Splenda, baking powder, and salt, then fold the dry into the wet. Fold in the blueberries and pour into the tin.
Bake 30-35 min, pulling it slightly underdone (it keeps cooking). Cool.
Stir the Splenda with the water into a glaze, spread over the cooled loaf, and chill 15 min to set. Slice into 8.

notes.text: 30-35 min is the ceiling — pull slightly underdone while the center still has a faint wobble. The Greek yogurt + protein batter keeps cooking as the loaf cools and goes rubbery fast if taken to a clean toothpick.
Fold dry into wet, not the other way: pouring liquid batter onto a mound of flour creates unmixed pockets of protein powder that don't hydrate evenly.

Frozen blueberries release more juice than fresh once thawed (freezing ruptures the cells) — if using frozen, fold them in straight from the freezer and don't thaw, or the bleeding juice turns the batter purple and the pockets muddy.
The Splenda glaze won't set like a sugar glaze — it stays soft. Chill 15 min to firm it enough to slice cleanly; if it stays tacky, add less water next time (aim for a paste, not a liquid).
Spread glaze only on a fully cooled loaf — on a warm loaf it soaks straight in rather than coating the surface, and you lose the white visual contrast.

steps.instructionText: Mix the butter, protein, oat flour, maple syrup, salt, vanilla, and chocolate chips with a splash of milk until it comes together. Press evenly into a parchment-lined loaf pan.
Melt the chocolate chips with the coconut oil and pour over the base, spreading into a thin layer.
Freeze ~10 min to set the shell, then cut into 5 bars.

notes.text: 90g whey + oat flour makes a very dense dough — the "splash of milk" means 1–2 tsp max. Over-adding milk makes the base sticky and the bars won't slice clean after freezing.
The maple syrup is the structural binder here; don't reduce it for sweetness reasons or the base won't hold together. If you want it less sweet, cut the chocolate chips rather than the maple.
Melt the chocolate chips and coconut oil together in 20-second microwave bursts, stirring between each — chocolate chips scorch fast, and a thin shell needs a fully smooth melt to pour evenly.
10 min in the freezer sets the shell, not the whole bar — cut with a sharp warm knife (run under hot water, wipe dry) or the chocolate shell will crack and shatter instead of slicing cleanly.
Bars taken straight from the freezer are rock-hard. Let them sit 5 min at room temp before eating — the oat-flour base softens to a cookie-dough texture once tempered.
