steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth — any visible curd survives baking and makes the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works well; a food processor needs 2 full minutes.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

payload.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt the butter in a light-colored pan over medium, swirling, until it foams, then smells nutty and the milk solids turn golden-amber (~2-3 min) - pull the instant it's amber, it goes from nutty to burnt in seconds. Off the heat, stir in the cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg and let them bloom in the hot butter ~30 sec - this is where the speculoos 'cookie' flavor comes from (brown butter alone is nutty, not spiced). Scrape it all, including the toasty brown bits, into a small bowl and cool to barely warm.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

payload.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt the butter in a light-colored pan over medium, swirling, until it foams, then smells nutty and the milk solids turn golden-amber (~2-3 min) - pull the instant it's amber, it goes from nutty to burnt in seconds. Off the heat, stir in the cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg and let them bloom in the hot butter ~30 sec - this is where the speculoos 'cookie' flavor comes from (brown butter alone is nutty, not spiced). Scrape it all, including the toasty brown bits, into a small bowl and cool to barely warm.
Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

Beat the fat-free cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, powdered peanut butter, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 45 g Biscoff, the cooled browned-butter spice mixture, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).

payload.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt the butter in a light-colored pan over medium, swirling, until it foams, then smells nutty and the milk solids turn golden-amber (~2-3 min) - pull the instant it's amber, it goes from nutty to burnt in seconds. Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

Beat the fat-free cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, powdered peanut butter, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 45 g Biscoff, the cooled browned-butter spice mixture, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

payload.text: Brown butter goes from nutty-amber to acrid-burnt in seconds. Pull it the moment the milk solids are golden and it smells like toffee; if it smells sharp or the bits are black, start over - burnt butter taints the whole cake.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).

payload.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt the butter in a light-colored pan over medium, swirling, until it foams, then smells nutty and the milk solids turn golden-amber (~2-3 min) - pull the instant it's amber, it goes from nutty to burnt in seconds. Off the heat, stir in the cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg and let them bloom in the hot butter ~30 sec - this is where the speculoos 'cookie' flavor comes from (brown butter alone is nutty, not spiced). Scrape it all, including the toasty brown bits, into a small bowl and cool to barely warm.
Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

Beat the fat-free cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, powdered peanut butter, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 45 g Biscoff, the cooled browned-butter spice mixture, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

payload.text: Brown butter goes from nutty-amber to acrid-burnt in seconds. Pull it the moment the milk solids are golden and it smells like toffee; if it smells sharp or the bits are black, start over - burnt butter taints the whole cake.

Bloom the cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg in the hot butter off the heat - the spices are fat-soluble, so 30 sec in the browned butter wakes them up far more than stirring them into cold batter. Brown butter brings the nutty caramel depth; the bloomed spices are what make it actually read as Biscoff.

This batter is leaner than a classic cheesecake (fat-free cream cheese), so it sets firmer and dries out faster - do NOT overbake. Pull at a just-set center with a slight wobble; chase a fully firm center and it bakes out rubbery.
Swirl the melted Biscoff on top, don't stir it in - a few toothpick S-curves keep a marbled pattern. Blend it all the way in and you just muddy the color and lose the 'Biscoff cheesecake' look.

Crustless by design - the Biscoff and browned butter carry the cookie flavor without a crust's calories. If you want a crust, the Protein Graham Crust sub-recipe slots in like it does on the other cheesecakes (about +50 cal/slice).

payload.instructionText: Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 40 g Biscoff, the toasted cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

payload.text: Toast the ground cinnamon in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant before it goes in - straight from the jar it tastes flat; toasting blooms its oils and is what makes the spice read as speculoos against the Biscoff. Stir the ginger and nutmeg pinches in with it off the heat.

This is a lean protein custard, so it sets firmer and dries out faster than a full-fat cheesecake - do NOT overbake. Pull at a just-set center with a slight wobble; chase a fully firm center and it bakes out rubbery.
The cooked pumpkin must be at room temperature before it goes in - even slightly warm, it starts cooking the eggs and leaves scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth - any visible curd survives baking and turns the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works; a food processor needs a full 2 minutes.

Toast the ground cinnamon in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant before it goes in - straight from the jar it tastes flat; toasting blooms its oils and is what makes the spice read as speculoos against the Biscoff. Stir the ginger and nutmeg pinches in off the heat.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 40 g Biscoff, the toasted cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.
Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin must be at room temperature before it goes in - even slightly warm, it starts cooking the eggs and leaves scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

a48e1ca0-4256-42ec-b433-821bcd7ee3d1.description: Biscoff cookie-butter protein cheesecake, crustless - a flavor variant of the Vanilla Protein Cheesecake base, built from pantry staples (no cookie-butter emulsion, no fat-free cream cheese, no powdered PB, no brown butter). 55 g Biscoff (40 g in the batter + a 15 g swirl on top) plus a toasted speculoos spice blend (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg) carry the cookie flavor. To stay lean without fat-free cream cheese, the base's light cream cheese is cut back (113 -> 85 g) and the body made up with blended cottage cheese (57 -> 110 g) + extra egg white (30 -> 60 g) - both lean and high-protein - landing at ~167 cal/slice (ratio ~10.9). To-make.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the Greek yogurt, milk, butterscotch pudding mix, and chocolate protein until smooth. Crush about half the cereal and fold it in.
Pour into candy-bar molds. Sprinkle the remaining cereal on top and drizzle with the zero-sugar chocolate syrup.
Freeze 6-12 hr until firm, then unmold. Makes 6 bars.

notes.text: The butterscotch SF pudding mix and 2 scoops of chocolate protein thicken fast once whisked — the 15 g of skim milk is the working liquid; don't over-add or the bars won't set firm enough to unmold cleanly.
Crush only about half the Ghost cereal into the batter; leave the top-layer cereal as full pieces so it stays crunchy even after freezing — fully crushed cereal just absorbs moisture and disappears.
Freeze the full 12 hr the first time to ensure a clean unmold — at 6 hr the yogurt center may still be soft and bars will tear coming out of the mold. Once unmolded, they can be stored in a bag.
Pull bars from the freezer 3-4 min before eating; rock-frozen Greek-yogurt bars are dense and hard enough to hurt a tooth — a short temper makes the center creamy without losing the shape.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the Greek yogurt, milk, butterscotch pudding mix, and chocolate protein until smooth, then fold in most of the chocolate chips.
Pour into candy-bar molds, press a few chocolate chips into the tops, and drizzle with the zero-sugar chocolate syrup.

payload.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt the butter in a light-colored pan over medium, swirling, until it foams, then smells nutty and the milk solids turn golden-amber (~2-3 min) - pull the instant it's amber, it goes from nutty to burnt in seconds. Off the heat, stir in the cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg and let them bloom in the hot butter ~30 sec - this is where the speculoos 'cookie' flavor comes from (brown butter alone is nutty, not spiced). Scrape it all, including the toasty brown bits, into a small bowl and cool to barely warm.
Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

Beat the fat-free cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, powdered peanut butter, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 45 g Biscoff, the cooled browned-butter spice mixture, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

payload.text: Brown butter goes from nutty-amber to acrid-burnt in seconds. Pull it the moment the milk solids are golden and it smells like toffee; if it smells sharp or the bits are black, start over - burnt butter taints the whole cake.

Bloom the cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg in the hot butter off the heat - the spices are fat-soluble, so 30 sec in the browned butter wakes them up far more than stirring them into cold batter. Brown butter brings the nutty caramel depth; the bloomed spices are what make it actually read as Biscoff.

This batter is leaner than a classic cheesecake (fat-free cream cheese), so it sets firmer and dries out faster - do NOT overbake. Pull at a just-set center with a slight wobble; chase a fully firm center and it bakes out rubbery.
Swirl the melted Biscoff on top, don't stir it in - a few toothpick S-curves keep a marbled pattern. Blend it all the way in and you just muddy the color and lose the 'Biscoff cheesecake' look.

Crustless by design - the Biscoff and browned butter carry the cookie flavor without a crust's calories. If you want a crust, the Protein Graham Crust sub-recipe slots in like it does on the other cheesecakes (about +50 cal/slice).

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.
Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin must be at room temperature before it goes in - even slightly warm, it starts cooking the eggs and leaves scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth - any visible curd survives baking and turns the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works; a food processor needs a full 2 minutes.

Toast the ground cinnamon in a dry pan 30-60 sec until fragrant before it goes in - straight from the jar it tastes flat; toasting blooms its oils and is what makes the spice read as speculoos against the Biscoff. Stir the ginger and nutmeg pinches in off the heat.
Don't overbeat once the eggs are in - mix on low just until smooth. Beating in air makes a lean cheesecake puff, then crack and sink, and it won't set to the dense texture this is tuned for.
A protein cheesecake sets firmer and dries out faster than a full-fat one - do NOT overbake. Pull at a just-set center with a slight wobble; chase a fully firm center and it bakes out rubbery.
Swirl the melted Biscoff on top, don't stir it in - a few toothpick S-curves keep a marbled pattern. Blend it all the way in and you just muddy the color and lose the 'Biscoff cheesecake' look.

Crustless by design - the Biscoff and toasted spices carry the cookie flavor without a crust's calories. If you want a crust, the Protein Graham Crust sub-recipe slots in like it does on the other cheesecakes (about +50 cal/slice).

Warm the 40 g batter Biscoff 10-15 sec until loose and pourable before it goes in - cold, stiff spread leaves streaks, and since you mix the batter gently (to keep the dense set) you can't beat the clumps out. The 15 g swirl is melted separately, just before it's drizzled on top.

3dad7cc0-fd22-4985-b3e4-4fee4030ea9b.description: Biscoff cookie-butter protein cheesecake, crustless - a flavor variant of the Vanilla Protein Cheesecake base, built from pantry staples (no cookie-butter emulsion, no fat-free cream cheese, no powdered PB, no brown butter). Keeps the base's PROVEN dairy ratio (light cream cheese 113 g + cottage 57 g + egg white 30 g - the same ratio as the excellent-rated Creme Brulee variant) for a dense, creamy set; 55 g Biscoff (40 g batter + 15 g swirl) plus a toasted speculoos spice blend (cinnamon, ginger, nutmeg) carry the cookie flavor. ~168 cal/slice, ratio ~11.8 - a bit richer than the leanest build, but texture is the point and it's still well under the Turtle (215). steps.instructionText: Mix the protein, almond flour, oat flour, butter, maple syrup, and lemon juice into a dough. Press firmly into a parchment-lined loaf pan; chill while you make the frosting.

Blend the cottage cheese, cream cheese, and lemon juice smooth. Melt the white chocolate chips with the coconut oil and stir in, then stir in the protein until thick. Spread over the cookie layer (thicken with more protein or cream cheese if loose).
Freeze ~20 min until set, then slice into 8 bars.

notes.text: Press the cookie layer very firmly — almond flour + oat flour with no egg binds only from maple syrup and butter. A loose press leaves a crumbly bar that falls apart when sliced.
Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth before adding anything else — any visible curds in the frosting won't disappear once the white chocolate and protein go in.
Let the melted white chocolate cool slightly before stirring into the cottage-cheese blend — if it's too hot it can seize or make the frosting grainy. Aim for warm, not steaming.
If the frosting is too loose after adding the 30g protein, add cream cheese a tablespoon at a time rather than more protein — extra protein powder can make the layer gummy after freezing.

Freeze 20 min to set, then move to the fridge — bars left in the freezer too long become rock-hard and the white-chocolate frosting can crack when sliced. Temper 5 min at room temp before cutting if frozen solid.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Brown the butter only to golden and nutty-smelling, then pull it off the heat - it goes from browned to burnt and bitter in seconds. Let it cool slightly before mixing so it doesn't cook the egg.
Stop as soon as the dough comes together - overworking the whey and flour turns these tough and cakey instead of gooey.
Don't skip the 30-min chill: it firms the butter so the tall mounds hold and spread slowly, giving thick centers instead of flat, greasy cookies.
Pull at 9-11 min while the edges are set but the centers still look underbaked and puffy - they finish on the hot tray. Bake until the center looks done and they'll come out dry.

c4b1c6cb-1a66-4dfc-adaf-13d8903d536d.name: Giant Single-Serve Protein Cookie
c4b1c6cb-1a66-4dfc-adaf-13d8903d536d.description: Yogurt-based high-protein cookie (no butter/sugar) found on Instagram, untried. Coconut flour subbed to oat flour; sugar-free chips to semi-sweet; 'zero cal sugar' to granulated Splenda. Chocolate chips unspecified in source — assumed 20g.

steps.instructionText: Mix all the ingredients together until smooth, folding in the chocolate chips last.
Divide onto parchment paper and press each into a flat round so it bakes evenly.
Bake 7-9 minutes until the edges are set but the center is still soft.
Let cool and enjoy.

notes.text: 7–9 min is a tight window — 170g of Greek yogurt keeps the center wet and it will look underbaked when it's actually done. Pull at 8 min when the edges are firm and the center is just set; it firms as it cools. Overcooking at this scale turns the whole cookie rubbery.
Press each portion thin and even — yogurt-protein dough barely spreads, so the thickness you press is the thickness you bake. Uneven pressing means one half overcooks while the center stays raw.
The dough will look thin and sticky compared to a butter cookie — that's normal at 37g protein powder with yogurt. Don't add more flour to compensate; it will bake dry and dense.
Let the cookies rest 5 min on the pan before moving — fresh out of the oven this dough is fragile. It sets to a handle-able texture as it cools.

payload.instructionText: Chill only ~15 minutes (or let cold dough sit 10 min at room temp before baking). A fridge-cold center lags the most, so less chilling helps the middle keep pace.
Shape into 3 cookies and flatten into discs about 1/2 inch (1.5 cm) thick.
Bake at 325F / 160C on the middle rack for ~11-13 minutes. Pull when set but the centers still feel slightly soft.

payload.text: Let the browned butter cool 2–3 min before adding eggs — pour it in hot and you'll scramble the egg and break the emulsion, giving greasy cookies with a curdled look.
325F for 11–13 min and pull while centers feel slightly soft — 40 g whey in a small batch overcooks in minutes, turning the center chalky. Carryover on the hot tray finishes them.
Stir in the dry ingredients until the dough just comes together; overmixing develops the AP flour's gluten and toughens the protein cookies into dense pucks.

Don't move or taste the cookies until they've rested 10–15 min on the tray — protein cookies feel floppy straight from the oven and firm up entirely as they cool; judging early will make you think they're underbaked.
The brown sugar (28 g real) provides the molasses chew and spread; the 3 g Splenda tops off sweetness without adding moisture, so the ratio is fixed — don't swap one for the other.

Flattening the cookie and lowering the oven temp both shrink the edge-vs-center cook gap, so the whole cookie finishes together. Spreads a little more, no molten center.

payload.text: Let the browned butter cool a couple minutes before adding eggs — 60 g of whey is already heat-sensitive; scrambled egg in the fat ruins the emulsion and makes the cookie grainy.
60 g whey is a heavy protein load for 3 cookies; add milk a teaspoon at a time only if the dough won't come together — too much liquid makes it spread flat and bake rubbery.
These stay pale — Splenda doesn't brown. Pull at 9–10 min when edges are just set and the center still looks underdone; waiting for any color means overbaked, dry centers.
The 10–15 min pan rest is where the centers finish cooking and proteins set. Moving them too soon means they fall apart; judging texture before fully cooled gives a false "gummy" read.
The 30-min chill firms the butter so the mounds hold their height and spread slowly — skip it and 60 g of whey in a small yield will spread flat and bake through before centers can stay gooey.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

payload.instructionText: Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, rolled oats, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. Add the splash of milk to bring it together so it holds its shape, not pours. Too stiff/dry -> a touch more milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Let it rest a few minutes so the oats hydrate, then taste for sweetness.

payload.text: Only 8 g of butter — it browns in under 2 min at medium heat. Watch from the moment it melts; the window between nutty and burnt is very short at this small quantity.
Let the dough rest 2-3 min after mixing before adjusting consistency: the oats and whey continue absorbing liquid, and what looks too wet will often firm to scoopable on its own.
9-11 min at 350F — pull while the centers still look underdone and pale. Whey protein bakes through on the hot tray; waiting for a set center means a dry, cakey cookie.
The 30-min chill is load-bearing with only 8 g butter: unchilled dough spreads flat before the edges set, killing the thick-center effect.
Don't judge texture off the tray — protein cookies are floppy when hot and feel underbaked. The full 10-15 min rest on the tray is when they firm to chewy.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the dry base — AP flour, whey protein, SF pudding mix, Splenda, baking powder, salt — until there are no protein clumps.
Add the melted butter, whole egg, Greek yogurt, and vanilla into the dry mix.
Stir to combine, then stop and let the bowl sit untouched 5 minutes so the whey and pudding starches swell into a shapeable dough. If still tacky, chill 5 more minutes.
Preheat oven/air fryer to 325F. Divide into 4 equal balls on parchment and press down firmly with your palm or a glass — this dough sets in the shape you give it, it won't spread.
Bake at 325F for 6-7 minutes. Pull the moment the edges look dry and set, even if the centers still look slightly soft — whey dries out fast.
Leave the cookies on the hot sheet 5-10 minutes; residual pan heat finishes the centers without making the protein rubbery.
Final step: rest in the fridge ~10 minutes to fully set, then eat.

notes.text: 6–7 minutes at 325F is aggressive — whey dries out faster than AP flour. Pull the moment the edges look dry and set; a soft center is correct at this point, not a sign they need more time.

The 5-minute rest after mixing is essential: the whey protein and SF pudding starches absorb liquid and the dough firms from tacky to shapeable without adding flour. Rushing past this step makes dough that spreads flat.
This dough does not spread on its own — press each ball firmly with a palm or glass-bottom to your target thickness before baking. What goes in is what comes out.
Leaving cookies on the hot sheet 5–10 minutes after pulling from the oven is the carryover finish — moving them to a cooling rack immediately stops this and can leave the centers underdone.
Pre-whisk the dry mix thoroughly to break up protein powder clumps before adding any wet ingredients — undissolved lumps don't hydrate evenly and leave gritty pockets in the finished cookie.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth — any visible curd survives baking and makes the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works well; a food processor needs 2 full minutes.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).

Pour about two-thirds of the batter into the parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Spoon dollops of the cooled berry swirl over it, add the rest of the batter, dollop a little more swirl on top, and drag a knife through in S-curves to marble - 3-4 passes only (over-swirling greys the batter). Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake in a WATER BATH at 300F (TEST): wrap the pan bottom in foil, set it inside a larger roasting pan, and pour boiling water halfway up the sides. Bake ~55-70 min until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly. The gentle, humid, low heat is the classic anti-crack method - if this finishes smoother and less cracked than our dry 325F bake, we roll the water bath out to the other cheesecakes.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

Make the swirl: simmer the mixed berries with the Splenda and cornstarch over medium heat, mashing, until jammy and thick (4-6 min). Off heat, stir in the imitation blueberry extract. Cool fully before swirling - hot jam melts streaks into the batter.
Once fully chilled, top with a scatter of fresh or thawed mixed berries just before serving.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth — any visible curd survives baking and makes the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works well; a food processor needs 2 full minutes.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

payload.instructionText: Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips and toffee bits. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.

payload.text: Toffee bits melt and re-set as crisp caramel pockets - press a few extra on top of the mounds before baking so they stay visible and crunchy. They add sugar + fat, so this runs richer than the plain chip cookie; we'll tune the amount.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips and toffee bits. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.

Bake at 330°F / 165°C - start checking at ~10 minutes to be safe (they may take up to ~15 depending on your oven). Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft - they stay pale, so don't wait for golden tops. Optional, for flatter, chewier cookies with crinkly tops: partway through (around the 6–7 min mark) slide the tray out and rap it firmly on the counter once or twice to deflate and spread the mounds (and again right out of the oven); skip it to keep them thick and domed.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Let the browned butter cool a couple minutes before adding eggs — 60 g of whey is already heat-sensitive; scrambled egg in the fat ruins the emulsion and makes the cookie grainy.
60 g whey is a heavy protein load for 3 cookies; add milk a teaspoon at a time only if the dough won't come together — too much liquid makes it spread flat and bake rubbery.

These stay pale - Splenda doesn't brown. Start checking at ~10 min and pull once the edges are just set and the center still looks underdone; waiting for any color (or the full 15 min) risks overbaked, dry centers.
The 10–15 min pan rest is where the centers finish cooking and proteins set. Moving them too soon means they fall apart; judging texture before fully cooled gives a false "gummy" read.
The 30-min chill firms the butter so the mounds hold their height and spread slowly — skip it and 60 g of whey in a small yield will spread flat and bake through before centers can stay gooey.

The optional pan-slap is the bakery 'pan-bang' trick: dropping the hot tray collapses the risen center so the cookie spreads thin with crackly, rippled edges and a chewier bite. Do it halfway and again out of the oven for the most spread; skip it entirely to keep these tall and gooey.

Toffee bits melt and re-set as crisp caramel pockets - press a few extra on top of the mounds before baking so they stay visible and crunchy. They add sugar + fat, so this runs richer than the plain chip cookie; we'll tune the amount.

Toffee adds sugar+fat, so we'll dial the amount (and maybe the protein load) for macros next.

d9e697e0-cb65-45da-b49c-f2079b2a83c0.author: user

payload.instructionText: Make the swirl: simmer the mixed berries with the Splenda and cornstarch over medium heat, mashing, until jammy and thick (4-6 min). Off heat, stir in the imitation blueberry extract. Cool fully before swirling - hot jam melts streaks into the batter.

Pour about two-thirds of the batter into the parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Spoon dollops of the cooled berry swirl over it, add the rest of the batter, dollop a little more swirl on top, and drag a knife through in S-curves to marble - 3-4 passes only (over-swirling greys the batter). Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake in a WATER BATH at 300F (TEST): wrap the pan bottom in foil, set it inside a larger roasting pan, and pour boiling water halfway up the sides. Bake ~55-70 min until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly. The gentle, humid, low heat is the classic anti-crack method - if this finishes smoother and less cracked than our dry 325F bake, we roll the water bath out to the other cheesecakes.
Once fully chilled, top with a scatter of fresh or thawed mixed berries just before serving.

payload.text: Foil-wrap the pan bottom so the bath can't seep in. Water bath + 300F = slow, even set with no surface overcook, which is what prevents the dome-and-crack. This is the recipe we're using to decide whether to convert all the cheesecakes.

The imitation blueberry extract is potent - 0.5 tsp is plenty; too much reads artificial. The cornstarch keeps the swirl from weeping into the custard. Toss the topping berries in a pinch of cornstarch if they're wet.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).

Pour about two-thirds of the batter into the parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Spoon dollops of the cooled berry swirl over it, add the rest of the batter, dollop a little more swirl on top, and drag a knife through in S-curves to marble - 3-4 passes only (over-swirling greys the batter). Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake in a WATER BATH at 300F (TEST): wrap the pan bottom in foil, set it inside a larger roasting pan, and pour boiling water halfway up the sides. Bake ~55-70 min until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly. The gentle, humid, low heat is the classic anti-crack method - if this finishes smoother and less cracked than our dry 325F bake, we roll the water bath out to the other cheesecakes.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

Make the swirl: simmer the mixed berries with the Splenda and cornstarch over medium heat, mashing, until jammy and thick (4-6 min). Off heat, stir in the imitation blueberry extract. Cool fully before swirling - hot jam melts streaks into the batter.
Once fully chilled, top with a scatter of fresh or thawed mixed berries just before serving.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth — any visible curd survives baking and makes the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works well; a food processor needs 2 full minutes.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

steps.instructionText: Whisk the dry base — AP flour, whey protein, SF pudding mix, Splenda, baking powder, salt — until there are no protein clumps.
Add the melted butter, whole egg, Greek yogurt, and vanilla into the dry mix.

Stir to combine, then stop and let the bowl sit untouched 5 minutes so the whey and pudding starches swell into a shapeable dough (if still tacky, chill 5 more minutes). Then cover and chill the dough ~30 minutes in the fridge — same as the browned-butter cookies: a proper chill firms it for cleaner shaping and a thicker, chewier bake.
Preheat oven/air fryer to 325F. Divide into 4 equal balls on parchment and press down firmly with your palm or a glass — this dough sets in the shape you give it, it won't spread.
Bake at 325F for 6-7 minutes. Pull the moment the edges look dry and set, even if the centers still look slightly soft — whey dries out fast.
Leave the cookies on the hot sheet 5-10 minutes; residual pan heat finishes the centers without making the protein rubbery.
Final step: rest in the fridge ~10 minutes to fully set, then eat.

notes.text: 6–7 minutes at 325F is aggressive — whey dries out faster than AP flour. Pull the moment the edges look dry and set; a soft center is correct at this point, not a sign they need more time.

The 5-minute rest after mixing is essential: the whey protein and SF pudding starches absorb liquid and the dough firms from tacky to shapeable without adding flour. Rushing past this step makes dough that spreads flat.
This dough does not spread on its own — press each ball firmly with a palm or glass-bottom to your target thickness before baking. What goes in is what comes out.
Leaving cookies on the hot sheet 5–10 minutes after pulling from the oven is the carryover finish — moving them to a cooling rack immediately stops this and can leave the centers underdone.
Pre-whisk the dry mix thoroughly to break up protein powder clumps before adding any wet ingredients — undissolved lumps don't hydrate evenly and leave gritty pockets in the finished cookie.

payload.instructionText: Once the cookies are set and cooled, drizzle with the sugar-free caramel (0 cal, so be generous) and a light sprinkle of graham crumbs. Chill briefly to set the drizzle.

payload.text: Graham crumbs in the dough give a golden-graham, s'mores-ish base; they also soak liquid, so if the dough turns dry add a tsp of milk or yogurt. SF caramel syrup is the lean drizzle (0 cal) - swap to the real brown-sugar caramel sub-recipe if you want it richer (costs calories).

payload.instructionText: Stir to combine, then stop and let the bowl sit untouched 5 minutes so the whey and pudding starches swell into a shapeable dough. If still tacky, chill 5 more minutes. Fold in the graham cracker chunks at the very end so they stay in chunky pieces rather than dissolving into the dough.

Once the cookies are set and cooled, drizzle with caramel and scatter a few extra graham cracker chunks on top. Chill briefly to set the drizzle. (Caramel = sugar-free syrup for 0 cal by default; see the note to swap in real brown-sugar caramel.)

payload.text: Break the graham crackers into rough ~1cm chunks and fold them in last for crunchy pockets (whisking them into the dry mix would pulverize them to crumbs). SF caramel syrup is the lean 0-cal drizzle; the real brown-sugar caramel sub-recipe is richer but costs calories.

43d92fd2-ef21-456f-abb6-98cbb552a17d.description: Low-flour protein sugar cookie tuned to kill the rubbery 'pancake' texture: one 33 g scoop of whey carries the structure with just 24 g AP flour, and SF instant pudding binds moisture for a dense bakery chew. steps.instructionText: Whisk the dry base — AP flour, whey protein, SF pudding mix, Splenda, baking powder, salt — until there are no protein clumps.
Add the melted butter, whole egg, Greek yogurt, and vanilla into the dry mix.

Stir to combine, then stop and let the bowl sit untouched 5 minutes so the whey and pudding starches swell into a shapeable dough (if still tacky, chill 5 more minutes). Then cover and chill the dough ~30 minutes in the fridge — same as the browned-butter cookies: a proper chill firms it for cleaner shaping and a thicker, chewier bake.

Preheat oven/air fryer to 330°F. Divide the chilled dough into 4 equal balls on parchment and press firmly with your palm or a glass to your target thickness — this dough sets in the shape you give it, it won't spread, so keep them on the thicker side for a chewy center rather than thin and dry.

Bake at 330°F. These are smaller and far leaner than the browned-butter cookies, so start checking at ~8–10 minutes to be safe — pull the moment the edges are set and the centers still look slightly underdone. They stay pale (Splenda won't brown), so never wait for golden tops: thicker-pressed cookies trend toward the 10-min end, thin ones can be done by 7–8. Optional, for crinkly tops and house-consistency with the other cookies: around the halfway mark rap the tray firmly on the counter once or twice (and again out of the oven) — note this does far less here than on the butter cookies, since there's only ~7 g butter and little risen mound to deflate, so it's truly optional.
Leave the cookies on the hot sheet 5-10 minutes; residual pan heat finishes the centers without making the protein rubbery.
Final step: rest in the fridge ~10 minutes to fully set, then eat.

notes.text: Whey dries out faster than AP flour, so this is a watch-it bake: start checking early (~8 min) and pull the moment the edges look dry and set — a soft, slightly-underdone center is correct and finishes on the hot pan. They stay pale because Splenda doesn't brown, so judging by color will overbake them dry.

The 5-minute rest after mixing is essential: the whey protein and SF pudding starches absorb liquid and the dough firms from tacky to shapeable without adding flour. Rushing past this step makes dough that spreads flat.
This dough does not spread on its own — press each ball firmly with a palm or glass-bottom to your target thickness before baking. What goes in is what comes out.
Leaving cookies on the hot sheet 5–10 minutes after pulling from the oven is the carryover finish — moving them to a cooling rack immediately stops this and can leave the centers underdone.
Pre-whisk the dry mix thoroughly to break up protein powder clumps before adding any wet ingredients — undissolved lumps don't hydrate evenly and leave gritty pockets in the finished cookie.

The 30-min fridge chill is the same firm-up the browned-butter cookies get: it hydrates the dough fully and lets you press a thicker cookie that bakes up chewy instead of thin and dry. Skip it and the warm, tacky dough presses thin and bakes through before the center can stay soft.

469fc281-3298-4610-91f1-0b4fb7b084e9.description: Base protein cheesecake (vanilla SF pudding, pumpkin for moisture/body). Launch point for flavor variants. Low-fat / high-protein; pumpkin does the work fat does in a standard cheesecake. Tuned DENSE (Tier 1+2): pumpkin reduced 120->75g + 2 tbsp AP flour for a firmer set (AP because that's what's on hand — its gluten sets denser than cornstarch), baked DRY (no water bath) to a just-set center and chilled overnight — denser at near-zero macro cost (~129 cal/slice, ratio 9.1). Stays lean; if a bake comes out rubbery rather than densely creamy, add a little fat (more cream cheese or an extra yolk).

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth — any visible curd survives baking and makes the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works well; a food processor needs 2 full minutes.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients into a bowl — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder, salt.
Add the wet ingredients — egg, melted butter, Greek yogurt, almond milk, vanilla — and mix to a dough. If dry, add the almond milk 1 tsp at a time until it just comes together.
Chill 20-30 min, then scoop onto a lined sheet, wet hands, and flatten (this dough barely spreads).
Bake at 350F for ~9 minutes — pull while the centers still look soft; they firm up as they cool.
Cool the cookies fully, then frost with the vanilla protein frosting (sub-recipe).

notes.text: 9 min is the target, not the floor — this dough has cornstarch, Greek yogurt, and 1.5 scoops of whey; another minute past "just set" edges produces a dry, cakey crumb instead of soft-centered.
Wet hands before flattening — the dough barely spreads and will stick to dry palms. Press to about ½ inch thick; thicker than that and the 9-min bake won't reach the center.
Greek yogurt and egg should be at room temp before mixing — cold dairy creates lumps in the dry mix and makes the dough feel stiffer than it is, leading to over-adding almond milk.
Fold the Cool Whip in gently first; then beat in protein and pudding on low — over-beating deflates the Cool Whip and leaves the frosting dense and sticky instead of light and spreadable.
Frost only after cookies are fully cool to the touch — even slight warmth melts the Cool Whip base and the frosting slides off the flat disk instead of sitting up.

e0590258-9f03-40c1-ab31-df17b2630fa8.name: Browned-Butter Protein Cookies
e0590258-9f03-40c1-ab31-df17b2630fa8.description: Browned-butter protein chocolate-chip cookies, makes 3. VERSION A - Thick & Gooey (molten center): tall bakery-style mounds, intentionally uneven (gooey center, firmer edges). The thick middle cooks slowest, so the edges finish before the center - that's the price of a molten center. Soft, fragile, and pale is CORRECT; these don't brown like a normal cookie. Confirm doneness by breaking one open after resting: soft/dense/moist/baked = done; wet/gummy/raw-flour = 1-2 min more. (Version B - Even & Soft-Chewy - is a derived variant that flattens + bakes lower for one consistent texture.)
e0590258-9f03-40c1-ab31-df17b2630fa8.author: user

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Brown the butter only to golden and nutty-smelling, then pull it off the heat - it goes from browned to burnt and bitter in seconds. Let it cool slightly before mixing so it doesn't cook the egg.
Stop as soon as the dough comes together - overworking the whey and flour turns these tough and cakey instead of gooey.
Don't skip the 30-min chill: it firms the butter so the tall mounds hold and spread slowly, giving thick centers instead of flat, greasy cookies.
Pull at 9-11 min while the edges are set but the centers still look underbaked and puffy - they finish on the hot tray. Bake until the center looks done and they'll come out dry.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.
Bake at 350F / 175C for 9-11 minutes. Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft. Stays pale - don't wait for golden tops.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Brown the butter only to golden and nutty-smelling, then pull it off the heat - it goes from browned to burnt and bitter in seconds. Let it cool slightly before mixing so it doesn't cook the egg.
Stop as soon as the dough comes together - overworking the whey and flour turns these tough and cakey instead of gooey.
Don't skip the 30-min chill: it firms the butter so the tall mounds hold and spread slowly, giving thick centers instead of flat, greasy cookies.
Pull at 9-11 min while the edges are set but the centers still look underbaked and puffy - they finish on the hot tray. Bake until the center looks done and they'll come out dry.

Yogurt kept for tang and protein. Sibling branch is the Crumbl-base version; bake both and promote the winner. Standalone root. Untested at this formulation.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 325F. Line a tray with parchment.
Whisk the wets - yogurt, pumpkin, egg, egg white, vanilla, food coloring, vinegar - then stir in the Splenda.
Add the dries - cocoa, oat flour, pudding, protein, baking soda, salt. Mix to a thick dough.
Rest 10-15 min to hydrate. If still batter-like, add oat flour 1 tbsp at a time until scoopable.
Scoop 5 cookies and shape into pucks (they barely spread). Bake 15-18 min at 325F until the tops spring back to a light touch and the edges are set.
Cool fully on the tray - they firm up as they cool.
Frost the cooled cookies with the protein cream-cheese frosting (see sub-recipe).

notes.text: The 10–15 min rest is necessary — oat flour hydrates slowly and the batter will look loose and unpipeable at first. Only add extra oat flour 1 tbsp at a time after the rest if it's still genuinely batter-like, not just soft.

These cookies don't spread — shape them into pucks at the thickness you want before they go in. Baking lower and longer (325F, 15–18 min) means the window between underdone and rubbery is narrow; start checking at 14 min.

The 1 tsp ACV reacts with the baking soda for lift — add it to the wet bowl last and mix quickly. Don't let the wet mix sit long before adding the dries or you'll lose the leavening before it hits the oven.
Cool fully on the tray before moving — oat-flour protein cookies are fragile and crumble when hot. They firm up significantly as they cool; moving them warm to a rack risks breakage.

The frosting thickens as it chills — if it looks too loose after mixing, don't add more pudding mix immediately. Refrigerate 20 minutes and check again; overly thick frosting tears the cookie surface when spread.

steps.instructionText: Mix the dry ingredients together — flour, vanilla protein, Splenda, baking powder.
Add the wet ingredients (egg, egg white, melted butter, almond milk, vanilla) to the dry and mix to a dough.
Coat your hands in flour to make the dough easier to shape; divide into 5 cookies on a lined sheet.
Bake at 350F for 10 minutes.
Allow the cookies to cool fully before frosting.
Mix the Greek yogurt, SF vanilla pudding mix, vanilla, and a dash of salt into a frosting; spread on the cooled cookies (add sprinkles to taste).

notes.text: 10 minutes at 350F is the ceiling — with 3 scoops whey in only 5 cookies, these dry out fast. Pull when the edges are just set and the centers still look slightly underdone; carryover finishes them.
The dough is thick; floured hands are essential — don't skip it. If it's too stiff to shape, work in almond milk a teaspoon at a time until it just comes together without sticking.

Don't frost until the cookies are fully cool — the Greek yogurt frosting will slide off a warm cookie and go thin. If the kitchen is warm, a 10-minute fridge chill after cooling helps the frosting set.
The SF pudding mix thickens the frosting as it sits — mix and wait 5 minutes before spreading; if it's too thick, thin with a drop of almond milk, not more yogurt.
Frosted cookies stored in the fridge firm up noticeably by day 2; let them sit at room temp 10 minutes before eating for the best texture.

steps.instructionText: Stir the graham crumbs, Splenda, and salt together. Work in the melted butter and egg white until it clumps like wet sand, then press firmly into the bottom of a parchment-lined 9-inch pan — run the parchment up two opposite sides as a sling so you can lift the whole cake out later. Bake at 350F for ~10 min, then cool while you finish the filling.

payload.instructionText: Caramelize the banana: slice and cook in a nonstick pan over medium heat with a sprinkle of sweetener until golden, ~2-3 min per side. Add the pumpkin to the same pan and cook 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. In the last ~45-60 sec, stir the ground cinnamon into the hot fruit to toast it — it should turn fragrant and deepen a shade. Toast it in the fruit, not in a dry pan: loose ground cinnamon scorches in seconds, but the fruit's moisture buffers it so it blooms evenly. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).

Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles. For the topping, toast the graham crumbs with the garnish cinnamon in a dry pan over medium heat ~1 min, stirring, until fragrant, then let cool. Scatter over the cheesecake after baking so they stay crisp.
Finish with sugar-free cinnamon syrup to taste.

payload.text: The cooled fruit is non-negotiable — even slightly warm banana/pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs the moment they meet in s4, giving you scrambled curds in the batter.

Blooming the 2 tsp cinnamon in the hot fruit (not a dry pan) is what the step says, and it's right: the moisture prevents scorching while the heat opens the aromatics — 45-60 sec is plenty, pull when it deepens a shade.
Don't overmix once the eggs go in — beating air into a lean cheesecake batter causes it to puff, then crack and sink. Low speed, just until the yolks disappear.

45 min is the ceiling, not the target. With cottage cheese + Greek yogurt this lean, pulling at 155-160F center (slight wobble, not wet jiggle) and letting carryover finish is what keeps slices creamy; a fully dry center = rubbery texture.
Scatter the toasted graham crumbs only after baking, just before serving — they absorb moisture from the filling within an hour in the fridge and go soft if added beforehand.

payload.instructionText: Cool the cookies fully. Whisk the drizzle (lemon juice + Splenda) smooth and spoon over the cookies.

payload.text: 9 min at 350F is the hard ceiling — these cookies will look underdone in the center and that's correct. Protein cookies firm dramatically as they cool; pulling at visual 'done' gives you hockey pucks.

The 20-30 min chill is load-bearing: it firms the butter and hydrates the cornstarch so the thick dough holds its scooped mound and spreads slowly, giving thick centers. Skip it and you get flat, greasy discs.

Granulated Splenda won't dissolve smoothly in lemon juice the way powdered sweetener does — the drizzle will be gritty unless you whisk it vigorously for 30+ sec and apply immediately before Splenda re-crystallizes.
The 15 g lemon juice goes in with the wet ingredients at b2; add it after the butter so the acid doesn't break the emulsion before everything is combined. Mix to a shaggy dough, not a smooth paste.
The drizzle is flagged 'needs-tuning' — granulated Splenda is the weak link. A swap to powdered Splenda (same volume) makes a noticeably smoother glaze that clings instead of beading.

payload.text: 3 tbsp cocoa makes this dough noticeably drier than the plain Crumbl base — don't judge hydration by how the plain version felt. Add almond milk slowly, 1 tsp at a time, until the dough just coheres; over-wetting leads to flat, spreading cookies.

payload.instructionText: Stir the graham crumbs, cocoa, Splenda, and salt together. Work in the melted butter and egg white until it clumps like wet sand, then press firmly into the bottom of a parchment-lined 9-inch pan — run the parchment up two opposite sides as a sling so you can lift the whole cake out later. Bake at 350F for ~10 min, then cool while you finish the filling.

payload.instructionText: Pour half the filling onto the cooled crust. Drop spoonfuls of the protein caramel swirl over it, add the rest of the filling, then drag a knife through in a few S-strokes to marble (don't overmix). Tap the pan on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Once fully chilled (ideally overnight), lift the cake out with the parchment sling onto a plate. Warm the caramel and the ganache separately just until pourable — a few seconds; they should ribbon, not run. Drizzle both over the top in a back-and-forth criss-cross (use a spoon, or a zip-top bag with a tiny corner snipped). Finish with a pinch of flaky salt. Slice with a hot, wiped knife.

payload.text: Mix on low after adding eggs — the 2.5 scoops of vanilla protein make this batter dense and prone to aeration. Overbeating here traps air that expands in the oven, then collapses and cracks the top.

Only 2-3 lazy S-strokes with the knife to marble the butterscotch swirl — more than that and you'll fully incorporate it, losing the pockets. The swirl should still be visible as distinct veins before it goes in the oven.

Pull at the first sign of a set edge with a slight wobble in the center (~155-160F) — with 2.5 scoops of protein this filling dries out faster than a traditional cheesecake. A fully still center means it's already overdone.

For a drizzle-consistency caramel (not thick), stop as soon as the almond milk is whisked smooth (~225F) and the sauce ribbons off a spoon — it thickens significantly as it cools, so pull earlier than you think you need to.

Add the almond milk WARM — cold liquid hits the melted unsweetened baking chocolate and can seize it into a grainy clump. A few seconds in the microwave before whisking it in prevents a seized ganache.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).

Pour half the filling onto the cooled crust. Drop spoonfuls of the protein caramel swirl over it, add the rest of the filling, then drag a knife through in a few S-strokes to marble (don't overmix). Tap the pan on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

6a058ea0-fb58-4cbd-8831-d6233f5b6166.description: Turtle protein cheesecake derived from the Vanilla Pumpkin base — pecan skipped, so caramel + chocolate carry the turtle identity. Adds a thin graham-forward chocolate crust (graham crumbs + cocoa, egg-white bound, minimal butter), a protein caramel swirl marbled into the filling (butterscotch SF pudding + 0% yogurt), and a top drizzle of REAL brown-sugar caramel + unsweetened-baking-chocolate ganache, finished with flaky salt. Splenda throughout, never monk fruit; the real caramel is the one honest-sugar indulgence, kept small. Bake in a 9-inch pan with a parchment sling for lift-out.

1b551e4c-d0a1-42cd-bd91-5771e906324b.author: system

payload.instructionText: Toast 65 g shredded coconut in a dry skillet over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until golden and fragrant (it colors fast then burns - watch it). Cool. Grind 45 g to a fine meal (spice grinder or food processor) and beat it into the filling with the wet ingredients in step 3 so the coconut disperses throughout; reserve the other 20 g for the topping.
Once the cheesecake is fully chilled, scatter the reserved 20 g toasted coconut evenly over the top just before serving (keeps it crisp).

payload.text: Shredded coconut goes from golden to burnt in under a minute — use medium heat and stir constantly; pull the skillet off the heat the moment it smells fragrant, as residual pan heat will darken it another shade.
Once the 2 eggs and egg white go in, mix on low just until smooth — overbeating whips in air that makes the cheesecake puff, crack, and sink, and with a lean cottage-cheese base it also turns grainy.

Grind the 45 g filling coconut to a fine meal (spice grinder, 15–20 sec) before beating it in — coarse shreds leave sandy pockets; a fine meal disperses evenly and gives a smooth coconut flavor throughout every bite.

Pull at 155–160F center or when there's only a slight wobble in the middle — chasing a fully set center with 2 scoops of protein powder and cottage cheese will result in a dry, rubbery slice. It firms dramatically overnight in the fridge.
Add the 20 g toasted topping right before serving, not before refrigerating — coconut absorbs moisture in the fridge and loses its crunch within a few hours of contact with the cheesecake surface.

steps.instructionText: Cook the pumpkin in a nonstick pan over medium heat, 3-5 min, stirring, until thickened and nutty. Remove and COOL COMPLETELY (hot mix will scramble the eggs).
Blend the cottage cheese completely smooth (immersion blender or food processor) - no visible curd, or the cheesecake turns grainy.

Beat the light cream cheese alone until smooth, then add yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, and vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined — don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.
Add the eggs and egg white and the cooled pumpkin. Mix just until smooth - do NOT overbeat once eggs are in (air = cracks, and we want a dense set anyway).
Pour into a parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake at 325F for ~45 min (or 350F for ~35-40 min if you want it faster) — NO water bath; a dry bake sets it denser. Pull when the center is just set with only a slight wobble (~155-160F center), not visibly jiggly. It firms further as it cools — do not chase a fully dry center, that is where a lean cheesecake turns rubbery.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

1b551e4c-d0a1-42cd-bd91-5771e906324b.description: Toasted-coconut variant of the vanilla base. Coconut runs throughout the filling (45 g toasted, fine-ground, beaten in) plus a 20 g toasted-coconut topping; crustless to stay lean-ish. Coconut is the only flavor source (the oil is neutral) so it is toasted hard for aroma. To-make; a tsp of coconut extract (0 cal) is the planned next lever to deepen flavor and drop the shredded amount.

fc61fbc2-89d4-491f-9f1f-70e801824cf7.name: Crème Brûlée Protein Cheesecake
fc61fbc2-89d4-491f-9f1f-70e801824cf7.author: system

payload.instructionText: Brulee the top just before serving (the shell stays crisp only ~30 min on the cake). Dust about 1.5 tbsp (20 g) brown sugar over the cold cheesecake in a thin, even layer. BROILER METHOD: rack at the top, broiler on high; freeze the cake 15-20 min first so the sugar caramelizes before the filling warms, then broil 1-4 min, rotating, watching every second - pull the moment it is an even bubbling amber, then let it set ~1 min into a crackable glass. DRY-PAN SHARD METHOD (no broiler): melt the 20 g brown sugar in a dry nonstick pan over medium heat, swirling (do not stir) until liquid and amber, pour thin onto parchment, cool until hard, snap into shards, and stand them on top just before serving.
Make and par-bake the graham crust (see the composed crust steps below), then cool it in the pan while you make the filling. The brulee filling gets poured over this crust.
Pour the filling over the cooled par-baked graham crust. Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Brulee the top just before serving (the shell stays crisp only ~30 min on the cake). Dust about 2 tbsp (30 g) brown sugar over the cold cheesecake in a thin, even layer. BROILER METHOD: rack at the top, broiler on high; freeze the cake 15-20 min first so the sugar caramelizes before the filling warms, then broil 1-4 min, rotating, watching every second - pull the moment it is an even bubbling amber, then let it set ~1 min into a crackable glass. DRY-PAN SHARD METHOD (no broiler): melt the 30 g brown sugar in a dry nonstick pan over medium heat, swirling (do not stir) until liquid and amber, pour thin onto parchment, cool until hard, snap into shards, and stand them on top just before serving.

Pull at a slight wobble in the center (~155-160F); a fully dry pick means it's already overcooked. This lean filling (cottage cheese + yogurt + whey) turns rubbery fast past done.
For the broiler method, freeze the assembled cheesecake 15-20 min first — the cold mass slows heat transfer so the 30 g brown sugar caramelizes to amber before the filling warms and weeps.
The brûlée shell softens within ~30 min on the cake; brûlée just before serving, not hours ahead, or it turns sticky and loses the crack.
