fc61fbc2-89d4-491f-9f1f-70e801824cf7.description: Creme brulee cheesecake on a graham crust: vanilla custard cheesecake over a par-baked graham crust, finished with a torched brown-sugar shell. A cheesecake is a baked custard, so the brulee crust is the signature; the graham base adds the classic restaurant form. The shell needs REAL sugar (sucralose will not caramelize) - ~30 g brown sugar in a thin even layer; everything else stays Splenda. Two finishes in the method: oven broiler (freeze first) or dry-pan caramel shards (no torch). About 183 cal/slice with the crust + bigger shell (was 140 crustless). To-make.

12c9eb9a-f78c-4d3a-883a-635082a82fcb.name: Fudgy Protein Brownies
12c9eb9a-f78c-4d3a-883a-635082a82fcb.description: The fudge-maximized protein brownie — the original of a three-texture set, finished smooth (uniformly fudgy) or chunky (sweetened dark-chocolate pockets). Fudge comes from butter + a little unsweetened baking chocolate, with the egg barely beaten and stirred in last to keep air out (air bakes cakey). Cocoa + espresso are bloomed in the warm fat; sweetener is 1/4 cup granulated Splenda (never monk fruit). Bakes at 325F for ~18 min, pulled at a slight center jiggle, then cooled fully and chilled — better the next day. Computed ~621 cal / 38 g protein per batch of 9; ~69 cal, 4.2P, 7.2C, 3.4F per square; 16.6 cal per g protein. Medium egg (44 g). Source: user.
12c9eb9a-f78c-4d3a-883a-635082a82fcb.author: user

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 325°F (165°C) and line or grease a small ~6-inch square pan.
Melt the butter + baking chocolate over low heat or in short microwave bursts. Stir in the cocoa + espresso powder to bloom them in the warm fat — it becomes a thick paste.

Stir in the skim milk to loosen and finish blooming; warm gently to combine. For chunky brownies, reserve 1–2 tsp of the thick paste, stir a pinch of Splenda into it, and set aside. Off the heat, cool to just warm.
Stir in the Splenda, then the Greek yogurt and vanilla.
Lightly beat the egg (no whipping — keep air out so it bakes fudgy, not cakey) and stir in last. If the base is still warm, temper first: stir a spoonful of base into the egg, then add it back.

Whisk the flour + cornstarch + protein powder + salt, then fold into the batter by hand just until no dry streaks remain — then stop. A few small lumps are fine; mixing past this develops gluten and bakes up cakey. Smooth finish: fold uniform. Chunky finish: fold in the reserved sweetened paste at the very end so it stays in pockets. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at a slight center jiggle (not a liquid slosh) — it should look a touch underdone; carryover heat and cooling finish the set.

Doneness: edges set and just pulling from the sides with a slight wobble in the center (not a liquid slosh). A toothpick should read moist crumbs clinging — a clean toothpick means overbaked. On these small protein batters, trust the jiggle over the toothpick.
Cool completely in the pan on a wire rack, undisturbed — never cut warm. The crumb sets and the protein firms as it cools; a warm one seems gummy and then comes good.

Chill a few hours or overnight — they're better the next day. Cut cold with a clean knife (for the fudgy ones, run it under hot water and wipe between cuts). Store airtight; freeze portions for longer keeping. Optional: microwave a piece 8–10 sec to soften the fat — no longer, or the protein turns rubbery.

notes.text: Don't whip the egg — just break the yolk and stir it in gently. Beating in air makes the batter puff in the oven and bake cakey; keeping it still keeps it dense and fudgy.
The cocoa blooms in warm butter + baking chocolate — let the fat cool to just warm (not hot) before adding the egg in step b5, or the egg scrambles. It should feel comfortable to touch.
18 min at 325°F is the max; start checking at 14 min. Pull at a slight center jiggle — not liquid, but not fully set. The protein continues cooking off-heat and the fudgy window closes fast.
If reheating a square, microwave 8–10 sec only — any longer and the protein in the Greek yogurt turns grainy and rubbery. Pull while it still feels just warm.
Stop folding the moment no dry streaks remain; the batter is small and 15 g of protein powder makes it easy to over-develop gluten. Extra strokes bake out the fudge into a tight, cakey crumb.

fc5520cb-3d2c-463d-9f41-763d02174910.name: Fudgy + Chewy Protein Brownies
fc5520cb-3d2c-463d-9f41-763d02174910.author: user

payload.instructionText: Melt the butter + baking chocolate (low heat or short microwave bursts). Stir in the cocoa + espresso to bloom into a paste; set aside to cool slightly.

Beat the whole egg + egg white with the brown sugar only until the sugar grit dissolves and it looks smooth and glossy — then STOP. This builds chew and the shiny top; do NOT whip it to a pale, voluminous ribbon, which aerates it and bakes up holey/cakey.
Stir the Greek yogurt into the egg mixture, then fold in the cooled chocolate mixture until uniform.
Whisk the flour + protein powder + salt, then fold in just to no dry streaks — then a few extra gentle strokes for a little chew, stopping before the batter turns smooth and stretchy. No cornstarch.
Stir in the Splenda; add a splash of skim milk only if the batter is stiff. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~17–18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at a slight center jiggle — it's fudgy-leaning, so on the early side.

payload.text: Let the melted butter + chocolate cool until just warm before adding to the eggs — pouring hot chocolate into the egg mixture scrambles it and you lose the glossy emulsion the shiny top depends on.

Stop beating the egg + egg white + brown sugar (22 g) the moment the sugar grit dissolves and the mixture looks smooth and glossy. Ribboning it pale and voluminous bakes up holey and cakey, not fudgy.
Only 15 g flour and 30 g protein here — the dry folds in fast. A few extra gentle strokes after the streaks disappear builds chew; stop the instant the batter feels smooth or starts to pull.
Start checking at 14 min, not 17 — pull the moment the edges are set and the centre has a slight wobble. A clean toothpick means overbaked; you want moist crumbs clinging. Carryover sets the centre.
Chill several hours or overnight before cutting — the fudge texture only fully sets cold. Run a knife under hot water and wipe clean between cuts for neat squares.

fc5520cb-3d2c-463d-9f41-763d02174910.description: The balanced one — derived from the Fudgy base, keeping real fudge from butter + baking chocolate but adding chew: the whole egg + an extra egg white are beaten with brown sugar until glossy (dissolved, never whipped to a ribbon), the cornstarch is dropped, and protein is doubled. 1/4 cup granulated Splenda, no added milk, baked at 325F for ~17-18 min and pulled at a slight (fudgy-leaning) jiggle. Medium eggs (44 g whole, 30 g white). Source: user.

Whisk in the neutral oil, then the Greek yogurt.
Bloom the cocoa + espresso in a small splash of warm skim milk, then stir into the batter.

Whisk the flour + protein powder + salt, then fold in to no dry streaks, then ~10–15 extra strokes to develop a little gluten for chew — still stopping before it goes very stretchy or tough. No chocolate, no cornstarch.
Stir in the Splenda; add a splash more skim milk only if stiff. Spread in the pan.
Bake at 325°F for ~18 minutes, checking from ~14. Pull at only a faint center wobble — chewy wants a touch more set than fudgy, but don't dry it out.
Whisk in the coconut oil (melted if solid), then the Greek yogurt.

payload.text: Stop beating the egg + brown sugar the moment it looks glossy and the sugar has dissolved — whipping to a pale ribbon traps air, which makes the top puff then sink and kills the chew.
Blooming the 18 g cocoa in 15 ml warm milk with the espresso deepens the chocolate flavor significantly — don't skip it or add the cocoa dry, which leaves a chalky note in a batter this lean.

The 10–15 extra fold strokes after no-dry-streaks are intentional and load-bearing for chew — they develop a little gluten. Stop before the batter goes stretchy or springy; that's the line between chewy and tough.
Start checking at 14 minutes — this is a small ~6-inch pan and 30 g protein + 25 g flour dry out quickly. Pull at a faint center wobble; a clean toothpick means overbaked on this batter.
Do not cut warm — the protein-yogurt crumb is gummy and tears when hot. Cool fully on a rack, then chill for a few hours; the texture improves dramatically overnight.

payload.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt the butter in a light-colored pan over medium, swirling, until it foams, then smells nutty and the milk solids turn golden-amber (~2-3 min) - pull the instant it's amber, it goes from nutty to burnt in seconds. Off the heat, stir in the cinnamon plus a pinch each of ground ginger and nutmeg and let them bloom in the hot butter ~30 sec - this is where the speculoos 'cookie' flavor comes from (brown butter alone is nutty, not spiced). Scrape it all, including the toasty brown bits, into a small bowl and cool to barely warm.
Melt 15 g Biscoff 10-15 sec until pourable and drizzle it over the top of the batter. Drag a toothpick through in a few S-curves to marble it - swirl, don't stir it in.

Beat the fat-free cream cheese alone until smooth, then add the yogurt, blended cottage cheese, protein powder, powdered peanut butter, sweetener, vanilla, lemon, the 45 g Biscoff, the cooled browned-butter spice mixture, and the vanilla pudding mix. Sift/whisk in the AP flour smooth (no lumps) and mix just until combined - don't overwork it. Warm the bowl ~15 sec if it clumps.

payload.text: Brown butter goes from nutty-amber to acrid-burnt in seconds. Pull it the moment the milk solids are golden and it smells like toffee; if it smells sharp or the bits are black, start over - burnt butter taints the whole cake.

Bloom the cinnamon, ginger, and nutmeg in the hot butter off the heat - the spices are fat-soluble, so 30 sec in the browned butter wakes them up far more than stirring them into cold batter. Brown butter brings the nutty caramel depth; the bloomed spices are what make it actually read as Biscoff.

This batter is leaner than a classic cheesecake (fat-free cream cheese), so it sets firmer and dries out faster - do NOT overbake. Pull at a just-set center with a slight wobble; chase a fully firm center and it bakes out rubbery.
Swirl the melted Biscoff on top, don't stir it in - a few toothpick S-curves keep a marbled pattern. Blend it all the way in and you just muddy the color and lose the 'Biscoff cheesecake' look.

Crustless by design - the Biscoff and browned butter carry the cookie flavor without a crust's calories. If you want a crust, the Protein Graham Crust sub-recipe slots in like it does on the other cheesecakes (about +50 cal/slice).

03885f6f-aaff-4cb0-9aad-9a55ea7b976e.name: Browned-Butter Protein Cookies (Toffee + Chocolate Chip)

payload.instructionText: Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips and toffee bits. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.

payload.text: Toffee bits melt and re-set as crisp caramel pockets - press a few extra on top of the mounds before baking so they stay visible and crunchy. They add sugar + fat, so this runs richer than the plain chip cookie; we'll tune the amount.

Calorie-swap, not an add-on: this trades half the chocolate chips for toffee bits (5 g + 5 g) so the cookie stays at the plain 60 g cookie's calorie level - chips and toffee are ~5 cal/g, so it's near 1:1 by weight. Shift the split toward more chocolate or more toffee to taste. Toffee melts to crisp caramel pockets - press a few on top so they stay visible.

steps.instructionText: Brown the butter: melt it in a pan over medium heat, swirling, until golden and nutty-smelling (3-4 min). Pour into a mixing bowl and let cool a couple minutes so it won't cook the egg.
Mix wet: whisk in the brown sugar, Splenda, whole egg, egg white, and vanilla until smooth and glossy. Don't whip air in - just combine.

Add dry: stir in the whey, flour, pudding mix, baking soda, and salt until a thick, scoopable dough forms, then fold in the chocolate chips and toffee bits. It should hold its shape, not pour. Too stiff/dry -> a splash of milk; too loose -> a bit more flour. Taste for sweetness.
Chill the dough 30 minutes.
Shape into 3 tall mounds - do NOT flatten.

Bake at 330°F / 165°C - start checking at ~10 minutes to be safe (they may take up to ~15 depending on your oven). Pull when the edges are set but the center still looks slightly underdone/soft - they stay pale, so don't wait for golden tops. Optional, for flatter, chewier cookies with crinkly tops: partway through (around the 6–7 min mark) slide the tray out and rap it firmly on the counter once or twice to deflate and spread the mounds (and again right out of the oven); skip it to keep them thick and domed.
Rest: leave the cookies on the hot tray 10-15 min after baking - they finish cooking from residual heat and firm up from floppy to chewy as they cool. Don't judge texture until fully cooled.
Fridge (optional): for a firmer, denser, chewier bite, refrigerate the cooled cookies 20-30 min or longer. Protein cookies tighten up when cold. Store leftovers in the fridge.

notes.text: Let the browned butter cool a couple minutes before adding eggs — 60 g of whey is already heat-sensitive; scrambled egg in the fat ruins the emulsion and makes the cookie grainy.
60 g whey is a heavy protein load for 3 cookies; add milk a teaspoon at a time only if the dough won't come together — too much liquid makes it spread flat and bake rubbery.

These stay pale - Splenda doesn't brown. Start checking at ~10 min and pull once the edges are just set and the center still looks underdone; waiting for any color (or the full 15 min) risks overbaked, dry centers.

The 30-min chill firms the butter so the mounds hold their height and spread slowly — skip it and 60 g of whey in a small yield will spread flat and bake through before centers can stay gooey.

The optional pan-slap is the bakery 'pan-bang' trick: dropping the hot tray collapses the risen center so the cookie spreads thin with crackly, rippled edges and a chewier bite. Do it halfway and again out of the oven for the most spread; skip it entirely to keep these tall and gooey.

651ddb07-5651-471a-9258-37e2d5bc2c55.author: user

payload.instructionText: Make the swirl: simmer the mixed berries with the Splenda and cornstarch over medium heat, mashing, until jammy and thick (4-6 min). Off heat, stir in the imitation blueberry extract. Cool fully before swirling - hot jam melts streaks into the batter.

Pour about two-thirds of the batter into the parchment-lined 9-inch pan. Spoon dollops of the cooled berry swirl over it, add the rest of the batter, dollop a little more swirl on top, and drag a knife through in S-curves to marble - 3-4 passes only (over-swirling greys the batter). Tap on the counter to level and pop bubbles.

Bake in a WATER BATH at 300F (TEST): wrap the pan bottom in foil, set it inside a larger roasting pan, and pour boiling water halfway up the sides. Bake ~55-70 min until the edges are set and the center still jiggles slightly. The gentle, humid, low heat is the classic anti-crack method - if this finishes smoother and less cracked than our dry 325F bake, we roll the water bath out to the other cheesecakes.
Once fully chilled, top with a scatter of fresh or thawed mixed berries just before serving.

payload.text: Foil-wrap the pan bottom so the bath can't seep in. Water bath + 300F = slow, even set with no surface overcook, which is what prevents the dome-and-crack. This is the recipe we're using to decide whether to convert all the cheesecakes.

The imitation blueberry extract is potent - 0.5 tsp is plenty; too much reads artificial. The cornstarch keeps the swirl from weeping into the custard. Toss the topping berries in a pinch of cornstarch if they're wet.

The gentle, humid, low heat is the classic anti-crack method - if this finishes smoother and less cracked than our dry 325F bake, we roll the water bath out to the other cheesecakes.
Cool: oven off and door cracked 10-20 min, then counter to room temp ~1-1.5 hr (max 2 hr out), then fridge at least 4 hr — overnight is best and gives the densest, firmest set. Best the next day.

Make the swirl: simmer the mixed berries with the Splenda and cornstarch over medium heat, mashing, until jammy and thick (4-6 min). Off heat, stir in the imitation blueberry extract. Cool fully before swirling - hot jam melts streaks into the batter.
Once fully chilled, top with a scatter of fresh or thawed mixed berries just before serving.

notes.text: The cooked pumpkin MUST be room temp before it goes into the batter — even slightly warm pumpkin will begin cooking the eggs in s4 and leave scrambled streaks in the finished cheesecake.

Blend the cottage cheese until completely smooth — any visible curd survives baking and makes the cheesecake grainy. An immersion blender in a tall cup works well; a food processor needs 2 full minutes.

Don't overbeat once the eggs are in — mix on low just until smooth. Beating air into a lean cheesecake causes it to puff, then crack and sink as it cools, and it won't set to the dense texture this recipe is tuned for.
Pull when the center reads 155–160F or just barely wobbles — it looks underdone but firms fully overnight. Chasing a dry, fully-set center in the oven is where this lean formula turns rubbery.
The staged cool (oven door cracked → counter → fridge) prevents the sudden temperature drop that causes surface cracking. Don't skip the oven rest or move it to the fridge while still hot.

Foil-wrap the pan bottom so the bath can't seep in. Water bath + 300F = slow, even set with no surface overcook, which is what prevents the dome-and-crack. This is the recipe we're using to decide whether to convert all the cheesecakes.

The imitation blueberry extract is potent - 0.5 tsp is plenty; too much reads artificial. The cornstarch keeps the swirl from weeping into the custard. Toss the topping berries in a pinch of cornstarch if they're wet.

651ddb07-5651-471a-9258-37e2d5bc2c55.description: FIRST DRAFT (to tune): mixed-berry flavor of the vanilla protein cheesecake base - a sugar-free mixed-berry swirl (punched up with imitation blueberry extract) marbled through the batter and a berry scatter on top. ALSO the test bed for a water-bath bake at 300F to get a smoother, less-cracked top; if it works we convert the other cheesecakes. Berries/extract are near-zero fat, so macros should stay close to the base - we'll confirm and tune when we talk it through.

9efc92c5-a533-4c96-bb6b-13f8f7efbd9f.name: Peanut Butter Cheesecake Swirl Brownies
9efc92c5-a533-4c96-bb6b-13f8f7efbd9f.description: Instagram import (reel DZ5M8gatrJw): a fudgy banana-based protein brownie layer under a blended cottage-cheese cheesecake layer with peanut-butter pockets swirled in. A brownie+cheesecake HYBRID like our Salted Caramel Cheesecake Brownie Bars, but the brownie is banana/cocoa/protein (no butter, no flour) instead of butter-fudge. Modeled faithfully as written (medium egg = 44 g per house rule); honey kept as written - house-lean swaps (honey->Splenda, peanut butter->PB powder) noted for tuning.
9efc92c5-a533-4c96-bb6b-13f8f7efbd9f.author: user

steps.instructionText: Mix the brownie batter: mash the banana, then stir in the egg, 1 tbsp peanut butter, chocolate protein, cocoa, salt, and baking powder until smooth. Spread into a parchment-lined pan.
Blend the cottage cheese, egg, honey, and vanilla until completely smooth, then pour over the brownie batter.
Dollop the spoonful of peanut butter over the cheesecake layer and gently swirl it in with a knife.
Bake at 180C / 355F for 18-22 minutes, until the edges are set and the center is just barely set.
Cool fully before slicing into 8 squares.

be5554ee-9bac-4d94-927f-9461eff7ba7e.name: Peanut Butter Cheesecake Swirl Brownies
be5554ee-9bac-4d94-927f-9461eff7ba7e.description: Instagram import (reel DZ5M8gatrJw): a fudgy banana-based protein brownie layer under a blended cottage-cheese cheesecake layer with peanut-butter pockets swirled in. A brownie+cheesecake HYBRID like our Salted Caramel Cheesecake Brownie Bars, but the brownie is banana/cocoa/protein (no butter, no flour) instead of butter-fudge. Modeled faithfully as written (medium egg = 44 g per house rule); honey kept as written - house-lean swaps (honey->Splenda, peanut butter->PB powder) noted for tuning.
be5554ee-9bac-4d94-927f-9461eff7ba7e.author: user

steps.instructionText: Mix the brownie batter: mash the banana, then stir in the egg, 1 tbsp peanut butter, chocolate protein, cocoa, salt, and baking powder until smooth. Spread into a parchment-lined pan.
Blend the cottage cheese, egg, honey, and vanilla until completely smooth, then pour over the brownie batter.
Dollop the spoonful of peanut butter over the cheesecake layer and gently swirl it in with a knife.
Bake at 180C / 355F for 18-22 minutes, until the edges are set and the center is just barely set.
Cool fully before slicing into 8 squares.

1d7e36d0-f873-4d00-b3f4-59295958e61e.name: Giant Single-Serve Protein Cookie
1d7e36d0-f873-4d00-b3f4-59295958e61e.description: Yogurt-based high-protein cookie (no butter/sugar) found on Instagram, untried. Coconut flour subbed to oat flour; sugar-free chips to semi-sweet; 'zero cal sugar' to granulated Splenda. Chocolate chips unspecified in source — assumed 20g.
1d7e36d0-f873-4d00-b3f4-59295958e61e.author: system

steps.instructionText: Mix all the ingredients together until smooth, folding in the chocolate chips last.
Divide onto parchment paper and press each into a flat round so it bakes evenly.
Bake 7-9 minutes until the edges are set but the center is still soft.
Let cool and enjoy.

notes.text: 7–9 min is a tight window — 170g of Greek yogurt keeps the center wet and it will look underbaked when it's actually done. Pull at 8 min when the edges are firm and the center is just set; it firms as it cools. Overcooking at this scale turns the whole cookie rubbery.
Press each portion thin and even — yogurt-protein dough barely spreads, so the thickness you press is the thickness you bake. Uneven pressing means one half overcooks while the center stays raw.
The dough will look thin and sticky compared to a butter cookie — that's normal at 37g protein powder with yogurt. Don't add more flour to compensate; it will bake dry and dense.
Let the cookies rest 5 min on the pan before moving — fresh out of the oven this dough is fragile. It sets to a handle-able texture as it cools.

beb6fa0c-0698-4ed5-8e91-9ce5cb4c84f1.name: Lemon Blueberry Protein Coffee Cake
beb6fa0c-0698-4ed5-8e91-9ce5cb4c84f1.description: A baked lemon coffee cake with blueberry pockets and a buttery crumb top, protein-boosted, in an 8x8. House calibration: the monkfruit/stevia blend is replaced with granulated Splenda. Bake until the center is just set with moist crumbs; cool fully before cutting into 9 squares.
beb6fa0c-0698-4ed5-8e91-9ce5cb4c84f1.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line an 8x8 pan. Whisk the flour, protein, Splenda, baking powder, baking soda, salt, and lemon zest, then mix in the eggs, milk, melted butter, lemon juice, and vanilla until just combined. Fold in the blueberries and spread into the pan.
Rub the flour, Splenda, melted butter, lemon zest, and salt together until crumbly and scatter evenly over the batter.
Bake 28-34 min until the center is just set and a toothpick comes out with moist crumbs. Cool completely before slicing into 9 squares.

notes.text: 28 min is the target; 34 is the ceiling. Protein powder dries out quickly in an 8x8 — pull the moment a toothpick in the center comes out with moist crumbs, not wet batter. Carryover keeps cooking it.
Mix wet into dry just until combined — stirring extra to smooth protein batter develops gluten and toughens the crumb. A few streaks disappear as you fold in the blueberries.
Do not slice while warm — a protein-flour cake is gummy and tears until fully cooled. Wait until the pan is cool to the touch; the squares come out clean.

Use melted butter (not softened) for the crumb so it clumps into distinct sandy pebbles when rubbed with the flour and Splenda — too much butter and it bakes into a solid crust rather than a crumbly top.
The lemon juice (2 tbsp) reacts with the baking soda — add it with the other wet ingredients and get the batter into the pan promptly; don't let it sit mixed.

ffeabc64-ff6e-44bb-8235-af319fd162d5.name: Biscoff Carrot Cake Protein Bars
ffeabc64-ff6e-44bb-8235-af319fd162d5.description: Soft baked carrot cake bars with Biscoff cookie butter in the batter and a cream-cheese protein frosting, finished with crushed Biscoff. Baked in an 8x8, cut into 12. A baked member of the Protein Bars family. House calibration: the monkfruit/stevia blend (batter and frosting) is replaced with granulated Splenda; the 30 g honey is kept (small, real moisture).
ffeabc64-ff6e-44bb-8235-af319fd162d5.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line an 8x8 pan. Mix the carrot, eggs, milk, Biscoff spread, Splenda, honey, vanilla, flour, protein, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, nutmeg, and salt until just combined; fold in the crushed Biscoff. Spread into the pan.
Bake 22-28 min until set. Let cool completely.
Beat the cream cheese smooth, then mix in the protein, milk, Splenda, and vanilla until fluffy and spreadable. Frost the cooled bars and top with crushed Biscoff. Cut into 12.

notes.text: 22 min is a starting check, not a target — with 90 g protein powder in an 8x8, the bars go from just-set to dry in a few minutes. Pull when a toothpick reads moist crumbs; the center will firm as it cools.
Grate the carrot fine (box-grater small holes) so it disappears into the bars rather than leaving wet pockets — coarse shreds can make the center steam and collapse.
The cream cheese must be fully room temperature before beating — cold cream cheese leaves lumps that protein powder won't smooth out. 30 minutes out of the fridge is the minimum.
Don't skip the full cool before frosting: these bars are fragile and gummy when warm, and the cream-cheese frosting will melt into them. Cool on a rack, then chill 15 minutes if impatient.
The Biscoff spread (60 g) adds real fat and sweetness — don't sub with PB or another nut butter without re-checking the batter consistency, as the fat ratio affects spread.

4474dfb4-f0f8-4e8d-a906-e89e7ba308c7.name: Birthday Cake Crumbl Cookie
4474dfb4-f0f8-4e8d-a906-e89e7ba308c7.description: A baked birthday-cake protein cookie: a Greek-yogurt + oat/coconut-flour dough folded with sprinkles, baked soft, then topped with a Greek-yogurt protein frosting set with SF vanilla pudding. A Crumbl-style copycat, but its own yogurt-based formula — distinct from the AP-flour-chassis Birthday Cake Protein Cookies that derive from the Crumbl Base. House note: maple syrup kept as written.
4474dfb4-f0f8-4e8d-a906-e89e7ba308c7.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line a baking sheet. Whisk the protein, oat flour, coconut flour, baking powder, and salt. Add the Greek yogurt, maple syrup, egg, and vanilla; mix to a thick cookie dough. Fold in the sprinkles.
Divide into 4 large cookies and gently flatten the tops. Bake 10-12 min until the edges are set. Cool completely before frosting.
Mix the Greek yogurt, protein, pudding mix, and vanilla until smooth and creamy. Frost the cooled cookies and top with extra sprinkles.

notes.text: Coconut flour is highly absorbent — it will keep thickening the dough as it sits. If the dough feels workable right after mixing, don't add milk yet; give it 2 minutes before deciding.
Room-temp Greek yogurt and egg mix in without streaks; cold yogurt straight from the fridge clumps against the dry protein and takes extra stirring, which risks overmixing the dough.
10 min is the floor, not the ceiling — pull when edges are just set and the centers still look slightly underdone. Whey + oat-flour cookies firm up as they cool; overbaked they turn cakey and dry.
Gently flatten each mound to about 3/4-inch thickness before baking — these don't spread much on their own, so the final shape is whatever shape you press them into.
Frost only on completely cooled cookies — warm cookies melt the yogurt frosting and it slides off. Even 5 minutes too soon makes a runny mess.

ba1f4314-87a8-4162-9029-04d6daf98445.name: Mini Cheesecakes
ba1f4314-87a8-4162-9029-04d6daf98445.description: Individual baked protein cheesecakes in cupcake liners: a buttery graham crust par-baked, topped with a Greek-yogurt + light-cream-cheese protein batter set with cornstarch, sprinkled with cinnamon sugar, baked, chilled, and drizzled with a sweetener icing. In the Cheesecake family alongside the full-size Vanilla Protein Cheesecake. House calibration: monk-fruit and Swerve brown sugar replaced with granulated Splenda (the icing Splenda blends smoother if ground fine).
ba1f4314-87a8-4162-9029-04d6daf98445.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F. Crush the graham crackers fine and mix with the melted butter, Splenda, and cinnamon. Press into cupcake liners. Bake 7 min, then cool 5 min.
Whisk the Greek yogurt, Splenda, cream cheese, egg, lemon juice, vanilla, cornstarch, and protein smooth. Scoop evenly over the cooled crusts.
Stir the cinnamon and Splenda into a cinnamon sugar and sprinkle over the batter. Bake ~20 min until set (not watery). Cool 20 min, then chill 30-60 min.
Mix the Splenda with a splash of water until drizzle consistency and pipe over the chilled cheesecakes.

notes.text: Don't overmix once the egg is in - beating air into the batter is what makes a cheesecake puff, then crack and sink. Mix on low just until smooth.
Bring the cream cheese and egg to room temp first - cold cream cheese stays lumpy and you'll overmix fighting to smooth it.
Pull them while the centers still jiggle like soft jelly (the middle ~1cm wobbles). They look underdone, but carryover heat sets them - a fully firm center means overbaked, dry, and cracked.
Chill fully (2h+, ideally overnight) before icing and eating - warm cheesecake is loose and gummy; the texture only sets cold.

51c63e2a-f098-49a3-ac74-39a2fa58de70.name: Lemon Blueberry Protein Bread
51c63e2a-f098-49a3-ac74-39a2fa58de70.description: A light protein loaf with blueberry pockets and a set glaze, baked in a loaf tin and cut into 8. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium. The 18 g light butter is replaced with 9 g real butter at matched calories. Pull it slightly underdone; it keeps cooking as it cools.
51c63e2a-f098-49a3-ac74-39a2fa58de70.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line a loaf tin. Whisk the egg, Greek yogurt, almond milk, melted butter, and lemon juice. Combine the flour, protein, Splenda, baking powder, and salt, then fold the dry into the wet. Fold in the blueberries and pour into the tin.
Bake 30-35 min, pulling it slightly underdone (it keeps cooking). Cool.
Stir the Splenda with the water into a glaze, spread over the cooled loaf, and chill 15 min to set. Slice into 8.

notes.text: 30-35 min is the ceiling — pull slightly underdone while the center still has a faint wobble. The Greek yogurt + protein batter keeps cooking as the loaf cools and goes rubbery fast if taken to a clean toothpick.
Fold dry into wet, not the other way: pouring liquid batter onto a mound of flour creates unmixed pockets of protein powder that don't hydrate evenly.

Frozen blueberries release more juice than fresh once thawed (freezing ruptures the cells) — if using frozen, fold them in straight from the freezer and don't thaw, or the bleeding juice turns the batter purple and the pockets muddy.
The Splenda glaze won't set like a sugar glaze — it stays soft. Chill 15 min to firm it enough to slice cleanly; if it stays tacky, add less water next time (aim for a paste, not a liquid).
Spread glaze only on a fully cooled loaf — on a warm loaf it soaks straight in rather than coating the surface, and you lose the white visual contrast.

abc7656b-4b8f-498e-83ec-6b96ed13c2cb.name: Carrot Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
abc7656b-4b8f-498e-83ec-6b96ed13c2cb.description: An oat-flour carrot cake baked in an 8x8 with a cream-cheese protein frosting, cut into 9. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium.
abc7656b-4b8f-498e-83ec-6b96ed13c2cb.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and grease an 8x8 dish. Mix the Greek yogurt, protein, eggs, applesauce, Splenda, and vanilla until smooth. Stir in the oat flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and baking soda, then fold in the shredded carrot and walnuts. Spread into the dish.
Bake 25-30 min until a toothpick comes out clean. Cool completely.
Whip the cream cheese, Greek yogurt, protein, Splenda, and vanilla until smooth and spread over the cooled cake. Cut into 9.

notes.text: 25 min is the floor, not the target — the 110g of carrot adds moisture and a lean oat-flour batter can look underdone at 25 min but carry-over finishes it. Pull when a toothpick comes clean and the edges pull slightly from the pan.
Grate the carrots fine, not coarse — coarse shreds don't hydrate fully in the short bake and leave wet pockets that make the center sink.
Cool completely before frosting — this cake is thin (8x8) and stays warm longer than it looks. Frosting a warm square melts the cream cheese-yogurt mix into a wet glaze.
The light cream cheese must be at room temp before beating — cold cream cheese stays lumpy even with yogurt and protein stirred in, and the frosting won't smooth out.
If the frosting is too loose to hold shape, chill it 20 min before spreading — the cold firms the cream cheese and lets the protein powder fully hydrate, giving a clean spreadable texture.

25a650a1-fdd0-4c0b-af0f-667aef091fd1.name: Apple Fritter Bites
25a650a1-fdd0-4c0b-af0f-667aef091fd1.description: Baked apple-cinnamon protein bites on an oat-flour/whey-isolate base, scooped and glazed. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium.
25a650a1-fdd0-4c0b-af0f-667aef091fd1.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 375F and line a sheet. Mix the eggs, applesauce, vanilla, and diced apple, then stir in the whey, oat flour, cinnamon, baking powder, and salt. Scoop into mounds with a cookie scoop.
Bake 12-15 min until golden. Cool slightly.
Whisk the whey, Splenda, milk, and vanilla into a glaze and drizzle over the warm bites.

notes.text: Toast the ground cinnamon in a dry pan 30–60 sec before adding it — straight from the jar it tastes flat; toasting blooms the oils and gives the fritter aroma you expect.
12 min is the target, not 15 — the whey+egg base dries out fast. Pull when the tops are just golden and a pick comes out clean; they keep cooking on the hot sheet.
The batter is thick from oat flour; if it won't scoop cleanly, work in milk a teaspoon at a time until it just drops from the spoon — don't thin it to a pour.
Glaze while the bites are still warm but not hot — it soaks in slightly and clings instead of pooling on a cool, dry crust. Add milk a few drops at a time if it's too thick to drizzle.
Splenda won't brown or caramelize the way sugar does, so don't wait for a deep golden color as your doneness cue — go by the pick and the bottom edges turning light gold.

462f3995-f23d-4e3a-bdc1-201c17459926.name: Carrot Cake Loaf
462f3995-f23d-4e3a-bdc1-201c17459926.description: A plain-flour carrot loaf with no frosting, baked in a tin and sliced into 16. House calibration: sugar-substitute is granulated Splenda (volume-matched; small maltodextrin calories counted); eggs medium; the olive-oil drizzle is coconut oil. NOTE: the first Batch entry mis-transcribed the source caption - baking soda was 4x (1 tsp vs 1/4), baking powder 2x (1 tsp vs 1/2), and oil half (1 vs 2 tsp) - which baked soapy/sulfury, eggy and gummy (logged bad). Corrected here to the caption amounts; the mixing + doneness steps were also tightened.
462f3995-f23d-4e3a-bdc1-201c17459926.author: system

steps.instructionText: Whisk the eggs thoroughly into the wet (Greek yogurt, milk, oil, vanilla, Splenda) until completely smooth and emulsified - no streaks of egg (uneven egg bakes into eggy pockets). In a SEPARATE bowl whisk the dry together - flour, protein powder, baking powder, baking soda, salt, cinnamon - so the leavening is evenly dispersed (a concentrated soda pocket tastes soapy/sulfury). Fold the dry into the wet JUST until no streaks remain - do not overmix or the gluten plus protein turn rubbery. Fold in the grated carrot last and pour into a lined loaf tin.

Bake at 350F (180C) until the CENTRE is fully set - a skewer in the dead centre comes out clean (a few dry crumbs OK; no wet batter or gummy paste) and the internal temp reads ~205F. Roughly 50-60 min for a filled tin; start checking at 45. Visual cues: the loaf pulls slightly from the pan sides, the top is matte (not glossy/wet) and deep golden, the split along the top looks set inside (not shiny batter), and the centre springs back when pressed. Tent loosely with foil if the top colours first. Do not judge by time or top colour alone - this is a moist batter and the centre lags.

Rest in the pan 10-15 min (it's fragile straight from the oven), then turn out onto a wire rack and cool COMPLETELY before slicing into 16. A warm protein loaf slices gummy and squashes; fully cooled it firms up and cuts clean. Even better the next day, wrapped at room temp. No frosting on this loaf — it's a plain spiced protein bake, sliced and eaten as-is to keep it lean; if you want extra, smear an individual slice with Splenda-sweetened 0% Greek yogurt (added at serving, so it stays off the recipe's macros).

notes.text: Grated carrot releases water as it sits — squeeze excess moisture out with a paper towel before folding in, or the centre stays wet and gummy even after the loaf is technically set.
Toast the 1 tsp ground cinnamon in a dry pan for 30–60 seconds until fragrant before whisking it into the dry mix — bloomed cinnamon punches significantly above its weight in a lightly spiced loaf.
60 g whey in a filled loaf tin dries out fast if overmixed — fold the dry into the wet just until no flour streaks remain, then stop. Ten extra strokes here translates to a rubbery crumb.

Start checking at 45 min and tent loosely with foil if the top colours before the centre sets — the matte/golden top and slight pan pull are reliable cues, but only a skewer in the dead centre confirms it.
Don't slice warm — a protein loaf fresh from the oven tears and reads gummy. Cool fully on a rack (minimum 1 hour) before cutting into the 16 slices; the crumb firms as it cools.

64ea0c9b-84d0-4033-94fc-e23f70545d9f.name: Birthday Cake Protein Loaf
64ea0c9b-84d0-4033-94fc-e23f70545d9f.description: An applesauce-based birthday-cake loaf with a Greek-yogurt protein frosting, finished with Fruity Pebbles at serving for crunch. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium. Birthday-cake-flavored protein is modeled on the vanilla-protein macro.
64ea0c9b-84d0-4033-94fc-e23f70545d9f.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F. Mix the Greek yogurt, applesauce, Splenda, eggs, flour, protein, baking soda, and salt; pour into a 9x5 loaf pan.
Bake about 50 min until a toothpick comes clean, tenting with foil halfway. Cool.
Whisk the Greek yogurt, protein, cake-batter extract, Splenda, and pudding mix into a thick frosting and spread over the loaf.
Top with Fruity Pebbles just before serving to keep them crunchy.

notes.text: 50 min is the ceiling — Greek yogurt + protein loaves dry out fast. Start checking at 40 min; pull when a toothpick has a few moist crumbs, not perfectly clean. The loaf keeps cooking as it cools.
Tenting with foil halfway keeps the top from browning before the center sets — Splenda doesn't protect the crust the way sugar does, so it can look done on top while the interior is still wet.
Don't overmix — once the eggs are in, a quick stir to combine is enough. Beating air into a protein-heavy batter makes it puff and then collapse into a dense, rubbery crumb.
The frosting thickens as it sits — mix it first, then let it chill while the loaf cools. A runny frosting on a warm loaf will slide off; wait until the loaf is fully cool before spreading.
Add the Fruity Pebbles only at the moment of serving — they turn soggy within 30 min on frosted yogurt.

ddd81630-7a3f-436f-b55c-1bff73f8fdae.name: Cosmic Sprinkle Protein Cookies
ddd81630-7a3f-436f-b55c-1bff73f8fdae.description: Fudgy chocolate protein cookies on a Greek-yogurt/pumpkin base, topped with a cocoa glaze and rainbow sprinkles. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium.
ddd81630-7a3f-436f-b55c-1bff73f8fdae.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F. Mix the Greek yogurt, pumpkin, Splenda, egg, and vanilla, then stir in the cocoa, coconut flour, and protein. Scoop into balls with an ice-cream scoop.
Bake 10-12 min until set. Cool.
Stir milk into the cocoa and Splenda to a glaze, top the cookies, and finish with rainbow sprinkles.

notes.text: Coconut flour is extremely absorbent — if the batter looks wetter than expected after mixing, resist adding more coconut flour. It thickens as it hydrates; let it rest 2 min before judging consistency.
Use a cookie scoop for uniform balls — the Greek-yogurt/pumpkin base is sticky and won't hold shape easily by hand. Wetting the scoop between cookies helps release cleanly.
10–12 min at 350°F is tight for a Greek-yogurt/protein cookie — start checking at 10. They're done when the edges are set and the center is no longer shiny; overbaking turns them dry and chalky.
Add the glaze only after the cookies are fully cooled — if they're still warm the glaze thins on contact and runs off. Start with less almond milk and thicken to a spreadable paste, not a drizzle.
Splenda-based glaze won't set firm like a royal icing — it stays slightly tacky. Keep glazed cookies refrigerated if not eating immediately so the topping doesn't weep.

83a5dc7d-6f09-4ab7-9f62-13b1ed35a5fd.name: Carrot Cake Protein Bars
83a5dc7d-6f09-4ab7-9f62-13b1ed35a5fd.description: Blended-cottage-cheese carrot bars in an 8x8 with a Greek-yogurt icing, cut into 9. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium. Sugar-free maple syrup is kept as the liquid sweetener.
83a5dc7d-6f09-4ab7-9f62-13b1ed35a5fd.author: system

steps.instructionText: Preheat to 350F and line an 8x8 dish. Whisk the cottage cheese, eggs, vanilla, and SF maple syrup, then mix in the flour, grated carrot, baking powder, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger, and salt. Spread into the dish.
Bake 25-30 min. Cool completely.
Stir the Greek yogurt with the Splenda into an icing, spread over the cooled bars, and dust with cinnamon. Cut into 9.

notes.text: The 25–30 min window is wide; cottage-cheese batters in an 8x8 can set as early as 22 min. Pull when the edges are set and a pick reads moist crumbs — a clean pick means they're already over.
Blend the cottage cheese smooth before mixing — unblended curds leave wet pockets that never fully bake through, and the texture reads lumpy even after cutting.
Don't cut warm — cottage-cheese bars are gummy and tear until fully cooled. Cool completely on a rack before refrigerating, then cut cold for clean squares.
Grate the carrot fine (box-grater small holes) at 55 g; coarse shreds stay chewy and release water pockets mid-bake. Pat dry after grating if they feel very wet.

The Splenda icing is thin when first mixed; spread it right before serving or it pools around the sides. If you want it to hold shape as a layer, stir in an extra tsp of Splenda and chill 10 min first.

7a60af4b-d3a7-49fc-a1cb-f47df14bf142.name: Blueberry Crumble Protein Bars
7a60af4b-d3a7-49fc-a1cb-f47df14bf142.description: A cooked blueberry filling between a protein crumble crust and topping, baked in an 8x8 and chilled before cutting into 9. House calibration: the recipe's sugar-substitute is swapped for granulated Splenda, volume-matched to its sweetness (Splenda's small maltodextrin calories are counted); eggs are medium. The 55 g cold light butter is replaced with 27 g real butter at matched calories; the 10 g honey in the filling is kept (small, structural).
7a60af4b-d3a7-49fc-a1cb-f47df14bf142.author: system

steps.instructionText: Simmer the blueberries, Splenda, honey, vanilla, and salt; stir in a cornstarch-and-water slurry and cook 4-6 min until thick and glossy. Cool 10-15 min.

Whisk the flour, oat flour, protein, oats, graham crumbs, baking powder, and salt. Cut in the cold butter to chunky crumbs, then fold in a mix of Greek yogurt, applesauce, egg, Splenda, and vanilla into a crumbly dough.
Press about 65% of the dough into a lined 8x8 pan; spread the filling; top with the remaining dough in clusters. Bake at 350F 34-38 min until golden and bubbling.
Cool fully, then chill 2 h before cutting into 9 bars.

notes.text: Keep the 27 g butter cold (straight from the fridge, cubed) and work quickly — if it warms and melts into the flour-protein mix you lose the chunky crumble texture and end up with a dense, uniform dough.

Mix the cornstarch slurry into the simmering blueberries off-heat or at a low bubble — high heat scorches it immediately. The filling should coat a spoon thickly before you take it off; it firms further as it cools.
34–38 min is the window; pull at 34 and check the crumble top for golden color. The protein powder in the crumble means the dough beneath will dry out and turn chalky if baked past set.
Press the base layer firmly and evenly — a light press leaves gaps that cause the filling to sink through when it bakes. Use the bottom of a measuring cup to compact it.
The full 2-hour chill is non-negotiable for clean cuts: the cornstarch-set blueberry filling and the soft protein crumb both tear and smear when warm. Slice with a sharp knife wiped between cuts.

4b45bf39-82ed-4114-951e-cf81f8571ffe.name: 7 Calorie High Protein Rainbow Cookie
4b45bf39-82ed-4114-951e-cf81f8571ffe.description: A recipe for high-protein, low-calorie cookies, yielding approximately 88 small cookies. House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. Imported via `batch ingest`.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
In a mixing bowl, add all wet ingredients and mix until smooth.
In another bowl, add all dry ingredients and mix.
Combine wet and dry ingredients.
Mix thoroughly until a thick batter forms, ensuring there are no clumps. Fold in mix-ins.
Refrigerate for 15 minutes to firm up the batter.
Prepare a parchment-lined cookie sheet or a baking sheet with cooking spray. Add batter.
Add toppings (optional).
Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes.
Remove when slightly underdone; they will continue to set as they cool. Cut into 88 blondies. Then enjoy!

notes.text: Stop mixing the moment no dry streaks remain — this is a Greek-yogurt/protein batter that turns dense and rubbery if overworked. Fold the rainbow chips in last with as few strokes as possible.
The 15-min chill firms a loose batter into something scoopable. Don't skip it — warm batter spreads too thin and the 88-cookie yield falls apart.

15 min at 350°F is the ceiling for this thin protein slab, not a target. Start checking at 12 min — a toothpick with a few moist crumbs is done; the pan's residual heat carries it the rest of the way.
Cool the slab completely in the pan before cutting — warm protein blondies are gummy and tear instead of slicing clean. 88 even pieces from a standard 9×13 means 8×11 cuts; score lightly first.

b12f4106-8c22-46d3-a82e-fd82ff1a4471.name: 99 Calorie High Protein Chocolate Chip Cookie Cake
b12f4106-8c22-46d3-a82e-fd82ff1a4471.description: A perfect cookie cake for your next birthday party, with a high protein and low calorie count. steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
In a mixing bowl, add the wet ingredients and mix.
In another mixing bowl, add the dry ingredients and mix.
Combine the wet ingredients with the dry ingredients. Mix thoroughly, avoiding clumps. Add the mix-in ingredients and mix again.
Chill the cookie dough in the fridge for 15 minutes.
Prepare a small/medium circular baking dish by lining it with parchment paper or spraying it with cooking spray. Add the cooled cookie dough to the baking dish.
If needed, wet your hands slightly and flatten the dough in the dish.
Bake at 350 degrees for 12-15 minutes. Remove from oven when slightly underdone, as it will continue to cook.
Let the cookie cake rest for 15 minutes. Optionally, decorate the sides of the cake with additional mini chocolate chips. Then enjoy!

notes.text: The Greek yogurt and cream cheese go in as wet ingredients — make sure both are at room temp or the cold dairy will clump against the butter and leave lumps that never smooth out.
Don't skip the 15-min chill: casein thickens as it absorbs moisture, and a rested dough spreads into a thick, even disc rather than pooling thin at the edges.
12 min is the floor, not the target — casein + Greek yogurt dry out fast. Pull when the center still looks matte and just barely set; it firms up completely as it cools on the pan.
Wet hands are the right call: the dough is sticky from the casein and yogurt, and dry hands will tear it instead of pressing it flat.
Splenda won't give a golden top, so color is not a doneness cue here — rely on texture and the 12-15 min window, not visual browning.

59245cf0-13f8-4565-83f0-fbe4c9573100.name: Caramelized Biscuit Chocolate Banana Protein Cake
59245cf0-13f8-4565-83f0-fbe4c9573100.description: A high protein, high fibre, flourless, no added sugar, probiotic, simple, macro-friendly cake layered with caramelised biscuit protein cream and a low-calorie biscoff and choc sauce. Perfect for satisfying chocolate cravings while staying on track with fitness goals. steps.instructionText: In a bowl, whisk your egg, then add mashed banana, cacao, and optional sweetener to taste. Mix until combined. Alternatively, add all ingredients to a blender and mix until smooth.
Pour into a greased large ramekin (12cm) and microwave for 3 minutes on high (900w) or until a toothpick test comes out clean.
Cool the cake, then slice horizontally to create two layers.
For the filling: in a bowl, mix your yogurt with vegan protein until combined and spreadable. Add some water if it’s too thick. Spread half of the filling evenly on the bottom layer.
Place the top layer back onto the filled bottom layer.
Spread the remainder of the filling on top.
Garnish: mix biscoff spread with water until you get a sauce consistency and drizzle over the cake. Optionally, add some no-added-sugar choc sauce or cacao sauce for extra deliciousness.

notes.text: Microwaves vary — 3 min at 900w is the spec, but check at 2 min 15 sec. A protein-banana mug cake goes from done to rubbery in under 30 seconds of overshoot; pull when a toothpick has a few moist crumbs, not bone-dry.
Cool the cake fully (10+ min out of the ramekin) before slicing horizontally — warm protein cake tears and crumbles. A serrated knife and a slow sawing motion keeps the layers clean.

The yogurt + 20 g protein filling is intentionally thick; add water a teaspoon at a time until it just spreads without tearing the cake layer — don't thin it to a pourable consistency or it runs off the sides.
Only 5 g of Biscoff spread is in play — dilute with water until it barely coats a spoon before drizzling, or you'll use it all on the first pass and the flavour will be uneven across 4 servings.

0140ea58-3ee3-4ea5-92e2-97dc9705e498.name: Flourless Coconut Greek Yogurt Cake
0140ea58-3ee3-4ea5-92e2-97dc9705e498.description: A naturally gluten-free cake that’s soft, moist, and made with just 7 simple ingredients. steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F and line or grease an 8-inch cake pan.
Whisk eggs until light and frothy.
Mix in honey, Greek yogurt, and vanilla until smooth.
Fold in coconut, baking powder, and salt.
Pour batter into pan and smooth the top.
Bake for 28–35 minutes until golden and set in the center.
Cool for 10 minutes before slicing.

notes.text: 28 min is the floor; pull at the first sign of a set center with only a faint wobble and a golden top — the 3-egg + Greek yogurt base continues cooking as it cools, and a fully dry center at 35 min will be rubbery when sliced.

Whisk the eggs until genuinely light and frothy — 1–2 min by hand — before adding anything else; in a flourless cake the egg aeration is the main structural lift (the bit of baking powder only assists), and skipping it gives a dense, flat result.
Use room-temperature Greek yogurt; cold yogurt mixed into warm frothy eggs deflates the air you just built and can leave cold pockets that bake unevenly.
Fold the coconut in gently — it absorbs moisture during the bake, so overmixing at this stage tightens the batter and can make the cake gummy rather than tender.
The full 10-min rest in the pan is mandatory — this cake has no flour skeleton; slicing while warm tears it. Cool on a rack and run a knife around the edge before unmolding.

4c2ab9ae-9d56-449a-b2ed-29c0721d018e.name: High Protein Banana Bread Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
4c2ab9ae-9d56-449a-b2ed-29c0721d018e.description: 4 x 350 | 38 c | 40 p | 10 f House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. Imported via `batch ingest`.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Mix bananas, eggs, Greek yogurt, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Add oat flour, almond flour, baking powder, baking soda, cinnamon, and salt. Mix until combined.
Pour the batter into a greased small baking dish.
Bake for 25–30 minutes, or until set.
Let the cake cool completely.
For the frosting: mix softened light cream cheese, nonfat Greek yogurt, vanilla protein powder, maple syrup or honey, and vanilla until smooth and creamy.
Spread the frosting over the cooled cake.
Slice the cake into 4 servings.

notes.text: 25-30 min at 350F is the range — pull when a toothpick comes out with a few moist crumbs. The banana + yogurt batter keeps cooking after it comes out, and oat flour dries fast when overdone.
Use very ripe, spotted bananas: underripe bananas are starchy and the maple syrup in the frosting will be the only sweetness, leaving the cake flat.
The cream cheese must be fully softened before mixing the frosting — cold cream cheese from the fridge leaves lumps that protein powder and yogurt can't smooth out.
Don't frost until the cake is fully cool — warm cake melts the cream-cheese frosting and it slides off rather than setting into a spreadable layer.
Fold the dry into the wet gently — overmixing oat and almond flour develops a gummy texture, and with whey powder in the batter there's no gluten network to save it.

9160abe2-e143-4551-a4b6-30a8d1001956.name: High Protein Birthday Cake
9160abe2-e143-4551-a4b6-30a8d1001956.description: A high-protein, lower-calorie birthday cake with frosting, perfect for dessert lovers who want to watch their intake. steps.instructionText: Mix all your cake ingredients together in a bowl and fold in sprinkles if using.
Pour the batter into one small cake pan or two mini pans (e.g., 4-inch).
Bake at 350°F for about 20 minutes or until the top is lightly golden.
While the cake bakes, mix all frosting ingredients together in a bowl until a smooth frosting forms.

notes.text: 20 min at 350F is the upper limit for a small protein cake — pull when the top is just set and a toothpick in the center has a few moist crumbs; oat flour + Greek yogurt turns rubbery if you chase a fully clean pick.

Mix wet into dry, not dry into wet — add the Greek yogurt, egg, milk, and butter to the bowl of combined dry ingredients and stir until just smooth; it avoids overworking the oat flour and keeps the crumb tender.
Splenda won't give the top a deep golden color — use the toothpick as your doneness cue, not color, and don't wait for browning that won't come.
Make the frosting first so it chills while the cake bakes — the Greek yogurt base needs at least 20–30 min in the fridge to firm enough to hold its shape on the cake without sliding.
Don't frost a warm cake — the Greek yogurt frosting will melt and pool. Cool the cake fully on a rack before applying.

695cff80-ff69-4f19-9e4e-0860bfe3f034.description: A single-serve, high-protein, no-added-sugar, low-carb, high-fiber, and gluten-free carrot cake that uses vegan protein powder instead of traditional flour. steps.instructionText: In a bowl, use a hand blender or whisk to mix the cake ingredients until smooth.
Add the baking powder and a splash of water, then gently fold to combine.
Pour the batter into a greased ramekin and bake in a preheated oven at 180°C for about 20 minutes.
Let cool slightly, then top with yoghurt, chopped nuts, cinnamon, and maple syrup.

notes.text: 180C for 20 min is for a full-size ramekin — check at 15 min by pressing the center lightly. With only 30 g vegan protein as the flour-stand-in, this single-serve cake overbakes quickly and turns chalky-dry.
Grate the 30 g carrot on the fine side of the grater, not coarse — fine shreds blend into the batter and soften fully in 20 min, while coarse shreds can stay crunchy in such a short bake.
Add the baking powder with the splash of water, not dry into the dry batter — in a batter this small, a dry pocket of baking powder can create a bitter spot and uneven rise.
Let the cake cool at least 5 min before topping with the 50 g Greek yogurt — warm cake makes the yogurt immediately runny and it slides off; a brief rest firms the surface enough to hold it.

058fc75b-bcca-4e81-8cdd-72f78ee92813.name: High Protein Coffee Cake
058fc75b-bcca-4e81-8cdd-72f78ee92813.description: Delicious coffee cake squares with high protein and low calories, perfect for a healthy snack. steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F and line an 8x8 inch pan with parchment paper.
In a large bowl, whisk together the greek yogurt, almond milk, apple sauce, egg, oil, and vanilla.
Add the protein pancake mix and protein powder to the wet ingredients and mix until just combined.
Set the cake batter aside.
For the streusel, add all streusel ingredients in a bowl and use your hands to combine until you get a sugary crumble.
Pour half of the cake batter into the prepared pan and layer half of the streusel crumble over the top.
Pour the remaining batter over the streusel and sprinkle the remaining streusel mix on top.
Bake for 30-35 minutes, or until a toothpick comes out clean but the cake should still be moist.
Let the coffee cake cool completely on a baking rack.
Mix the icing ingredients together and drizzle over the top of the cooled coffee cake.
Slice and enjoy!

notes.text: A clean toothpick here means overbaked — this protein + Greek yogurt batter dries out quickly. Pull at 30 min when a pick comes out with a few moist crumbs; the cake firms as it cools.
Use cold butter for the streusel: cold fat cuts into the dry ingredients in clumps that stay crumbly during baking. Room-temp butter melts flat and loses the crunchy layer.
Press the first streusel layer down lightly with your fingers before adding the second batter pour — loose crumbs float up into the batter and lose definition between the layers.
Mix just until combined when adding protein pancake mix and protein powder to the wet ingredients — both contain leaveners and overmixing deflates the batter and makes the crumb dense.
Cool completely on the rack before drizzling the icing — a warm cake makes the Splenda icing soak in rather than set on the surface. The icing firms nicely in about 5 min on a fully cooled cake.

4afd4642-24b1-467f-8398-6a358f4d7761.description: A light and fluffy honey vanilla cake, made healthier with Greek yogurt frosting. steps.instructionText: In separate bowls, mix the wet ingredients and the dry ingredients.
Combine the wet and dry mixtures together.
Fill a springform pan no more than halfway up. The pan size can be 5, 6, or 7 inches.
Bake at 305°F for 15 minutes. The baking temperature is lower because the oven runs hot. After 15 minutes, cover the cake with aluminum foil and bake for another 8 minutes.
Remove the cake from the oven and let it cool in the pan for at least 15 minutes without disturbing it.
While the cake is cooling, prepare the frosting by mixing the frosting ingredients until the mixture is thick.
Spread the frosting over the cooled cake.
Enjoy your cake!

Chef’s Note: To make removal easier, line your springform pan with cooking spray and parchment paper. Cut parchment paper to fit the bottom, spray the bottom to help it stick, and then spray the sides.

notes.text: Cream the 113 g butter with the Splenda and honey first until pale, then add eggs one at a time — this builds structure so the Greek yogurt and protein fold in without deflating or curdling the batter.
With 2 scoops of whey in the batter, overmixing after combining wet and dry produces a rubbery, dense crumb. Fold until just no dry streaks remain and stop immediately.

305°F is deliberately low — don't bump the temperature. At a normal 350°F the protein sets the outside fast while the 3-egg interior stays wet, then cracks. The foil tent at 15 min prevents the top from over-browning during the final 8 minutes.
Don't skip the 15-minute in-pan rest — this cake is fragile warm and will tear if released from the springform too soon. Let it cool in the pan undisturbed before running the ring.

The Greek yogurt frosting is thickened by the casein (sl3) — it will firm up as it sits. Mix it just before frosting; if it thickens too much to spread, a tiny splash of milk loosens it without breaking it.

0e7f22ee-623e-49d8-8e15-fa19f260be49.name: Low-Calorie, High-Protein Coconut Cake
0e7f22ee-623e-49d8-8e15-fa19f260be49.description: A delicious and guilt-free low-calorie, high-protein coconut cake, perfect for any occasion, especially Easter. steps.instructionText: Mix all the cake ingredients together.
Pour the batter evenly into lined 6-inch cake tins.
Bake at 350°F for 20-25 minutes. Do not overbake! Keep an eye on it and use a toothpick to check for doneness.
Allow the cake to cool completely before mixing the frosting and assembling. It is usually best to wait a whole day before decorating and putting it all together.
Enjoy your delicious low-calorie, high-protein coconut cake!

notes.text: 20–25 min at 350°F is tight for a whey + applesauce batter — start checking at 18 min. Pull when a toothpick reads a few moist crumbs; a clean pick means the crumb is already drying out.
Bring the Greek yogurt (both the cake and frosting portions) to room temp before mixing — cold yogurt clumps around the protein powder and leaves dry lumps that don't bake out.

The frosting is Greek yogurt + light cream cheese — it will weep and slide off a warm cake. Wait until the cake is fully cooled (or even chilled overnight) before assembling; the step's advice here is worth following.

The baking soda (1 tsp) is a strong leavener for a thin 6-inch tin — don't add more thinking it'll help rise. Too much makes the center dome and crack aggressively, and the alkalinity dulls the coconut flavor.
Make the frosting first and chill it 10–15 min before spreading. The cold cream cheese is what firms it up, so it pipes and spreads cleanly once set rather than weeping off the cake.

a8fb7483-6494-40c1-a22a-c4c239bb1463.name: Protein Carrot Cake
a8fb7483-6494-40c1-a22a-c4c239bb1463.description: A protein-packed carrot cake — about 575 cal and 79 g protein for the whole cake (6 slices ≈ 96 cal, 13 g protein, 1 g fat each). Tuned with 1 tsp apple cider vinegar + ½ tsp baking soda for a softer, higher-rising crumb. House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. Imported via `batch ingest`.
a8fb7483-6494-40c1-a22a-c4c239bb1463.author: system

steps.instructionText: Prepare the carrots by grating them.
In a large bowl, combine the grated carrots, nonfat Greek yogurt, egg, protein powder, banana, baking powder, cinnamon, vanilla, and sweetener.
Mix all ingredients thoroughly until well combined.
Pour the batter into a prepared baking dish or individual ramekins.
Bake in a preheated oven at 180°C (350°F) for 30 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean.
Let the cake cool slightly before serving.

notes.text: 30 min at 180°C is the target for the full baking dish — individual ramekins will be done in 18–22 min. A toothpick that comes out clean is the real signal; pulling by time alone risks a dry, rubbery crumb from the 2 scoops of whey.

Add the baking soda and ACV (1 tsp) directly to the wet bowl rather than pre-mixing with dry — they need to react in the batter to give this no-flour cake its lift; mixing soda into the dry first kills that reaction.
Grate carrots fine, not coarse — coarse shreds in a low-fat, egg-light batter stay hard and don't integrate; fine grating releases moisture that helps bind the 2-scoop protein load.
"Cool slightly" isn't enough — this cake has no fat and 2 scoops of whey; cut while warm and it tears and falls apart. Cool at least 15 min, or fully to room temp for clean slices.
The 75 g banana is doing double duty as binder and natural sweetener alongside Splenda — use a ripe (spotted) banana; underripe banana adds starch without sweetness and throws off the balance.

9109f3dd-48e2-4dd1-9516-a2668f122129.name: Protein Cookie Dough Cookies
9109f3dd-48e2-4dd1-9516-a2668f122129.description: Delicious and high-protein cookie dough cookies, perfect for a healthier dessert option. House calibration: the cookie-dough dough and crumble topping use REAL brown sugar for the molasses chew that defines cookie dough; the frosting and other sugar-substitutes are granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter is real butter at matched calories. Imported via batch ingest.
9109f3dd-48e2-4dd1-9516-a2668f122129.author: system

steps.instructionText: In a large bowl, combine the flour, vanilla protein powder, brown sugar, baking powder, and salt. Mix well.
Add the egg, melted light butter, Greek yogurt, vanilla extract, and almond milk to the dry ingredients. Mix until just combined and a dough forms. Be careful not to overmix.
Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C).
Scoop the dough using an ice cream scooper and place onto a baking sheet lined with parchment paper.
Bake for 8-10 minutes. Remove from the oven when the tops still look slightly undercooked, as they will continue to set as they cool.

While the cookies are cooling, prepare the frosting by mixing the Greek yogurt, zero sugar Cool Whip, vanilla protein powder, sugar-free vanilla pudding mix, sweetener, and salt in a bowl until smooth and creamy. Place the frosting in the refrigerator.
For the cookie dough topping, combine the oat flour, vanilla protein powder, brown sugar, vanilla extract, and salt in a separate bowl.
Slowly add almond milk, a little at a time, until a cookie dough texture forms. Roll this mixture into 21 tiny balls.
Frost each cooled cookie with the prepared frosting.
Top each frosted cookie with the tiny cookie dough balls and chocolate chips. Enjoy!

notes.text: Pull at 8–9 min when tops look slightly underdone — the Greek yogurt + protein base sets firm on cooling. 10 min is the hard ceiling; a fully dry-looking top at the oven means rubbery cookies by the time they're frosted.
Stir wet into dry just until a dough forms and stop — extra mixing builds gluten in the AP flour and makes the cookie base tough rather than tender.

Add almond milk to the cookie-dough topping a teaspoon at a time: the oat flour + protein mixture absorbs slowly and you can easily go from crumbly to too soft in one splash. Stop when it holds a ball without sticking to your hands.
Only frost completely cooled cookies — the Greek yogurt frosting is thin enough to melt and run on a warm base, and won't set back up once it does.
The frosting firms in the fridge and loosens at room temp; if it's sitting out while you frost all 6 cookies it may thin — a 5-min back-in-the-fridge rest restores the right texture.

54ed288b-1d47-418d-9b7c-eb53b532c840.name: Protein Kinder Cookies
54ed288b-1d47-418d-9b7c-eb53b532c840.description: These are described as 'MY BEST COOKIES EVER!!!' and are protein-enhanced cookies with kinder slices. steps.instructionText: Mix everything together to form the dough.
Bake at 350°F for 7-8 minutes.

notes.text: Coconut flour absorbs moisture aggressively and walnuts add bulk — the dough will stiffen within 2 minutes of mixing. Don't judge spreadability immediately; let it rest a moment, then portion.

Mix nut butter (walnuts here are the structural binder) and egg together first until fully emulsified before adding the dry ingredients — this prevents dry pockets of protein powder in the finished cookie.

7–8 min at 350°F is the ceiling for 6 cookies this size — pull when edges are just set and centres still look slightly underdone. The Kinder chocolate holds residual heat and the protein finishes cooking on the pan.

Press the Kinder slices gently into the tops right before baking rather than mixing them into the dough — they stay whole, melt slightly into the surface, and look clean rather than disappearing into the cookie.

1 tsp baking soda (4.6 g) is assertive for 6 small cookies — expect a slight lift and a touch of soda flavour if underbaked. Don't under-mix or you'll get concentrated soda pockets; mix until the dough is completely uniform.

048e9e2b-06a5-42e1-973f-c5fd4d7da8fb.name: Protein S'mores Brownies
048e9e2b-06a5-42e1-973f-c5fd4d7da8fb.description: Need S’more protein? Try these healthy brownies with a s'mores twist. Features a graham cracker base, fudgy brownie layer, and a creamy frosting. Macros per brownie: ~320 calories, 26g protein. House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Crush graham crackers and mix with maple syrup. Press this mixture onto the bottom of a 9x5 loaf pan.
Combine all brownie ingredients in a bowl and mix well. Spread this batter evenly over the graham cracker base.
Bake for approximately 45 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted into the center comes out clean. Be careful not to overbake, as this can affect the fudgy texture.
While the brownies bake, prepare the frosting by mixing all frosting ingredients together until smooth. If using pudding mix, add it to thicken the frosting.
Once the brownies have cooled slightly, spread the frosting evenly over the top.

Sprinkle crushed graham crackers over the frosting. If desired, prepare the chocolate drizzle by melting the oil and chocolate together in the microwave in 30-second intervals until smooth, then drizzle over the brownies.
Cut the brownies into four pieces to create squares. For the best texture and flavor, chill the brownies in the refrigerator before serving.

notes.text: 45 min is dangerously long for a Greek yogurt + pumpkin batter — check at 30 min. Pull when a pick reads moist crumbs; the pumpkin holds moisture but the protein still turns rubbery if pushed past set.
The graham base needs firm pressing — pack it tightly with the bottom of a measuring cup so it holds together as a layer when you pour batter on top. A loose base crumbles when you cut the squares.
The step says 'cooled slightly' but the yogurt frosting will melt and slide on a warm brownie. Wait until the pan is fully cool to the touch before spreading — at least 30 min on a rack.
For the chocolate drizzle, melt the 3 tbsp coconut oil with chocolate in 30-sec microwave bursts and stir between each — coconut oil separates quickly and scorches if microwaved all at once.
Chill before cutting — this layered brownie (graham base + pumpkin-protein body + frosting) holds together cleanly only when cold. Warm, the layers slide and the bars fall apart.

05a385fb-de2f-4735-ab55-d7499588c9dc.name: S'mores Cake Bars
05a385fb-de2f-4735-ab55-d7499588c9dc.description: Childhood s'mores flavor recreated in perfect little cake bars, offering nostalgia with a healthier, protein-packed twist. Ideal for a summer treat. House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. Imported via `batch ingest`.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F and line an 8x8 pan with parchment paper or spray.
In a bowl, combine all of your ingredients for the base until well combined.
Spread the batter into your prepared pan.
Bake for 20–24 minutes or until the center is just set.
Top with mini marshmallows, extra chocolate chunks, and crushed graham crackers.
Broil for 30–60 seconds VERY carefully until golden and toasted.
Allow for them to cool and then slice and enjoy!

notes.text: Pull at 20 min and check: a toothpick should come out with a few moist crumbs. The protein + applesauce + marshmallow fluff base goes from just-set to dry and rubbery quickly — 24 min is the hard ceiling.
Stay at the oven for the entire 30–60 second broil and watch through the glass — mini marshmallows go from golden to charred in seconds and there's no recovering burnt sugar on top of baked bars.

Mix the wet ingredients (eggs, applesauce, milk, marshmallow fluff, butter, maple) first until combined before adding the dry — the marshmallow fluff clumps stubbornly if it meets dry flour without being loosened first.
Cool fully before slicing — the marshmallow topping is still tacky and the bar interior gummy when warm. 20–30 min on a rack; patience prevents torn tops and smeared chocolate.

Add the chocolate chunks and graham topping right after pulling from the oven (before broiling), not after — the residual heat from the bars slightly softens the chocolate chunks so they nestle in rather than sitting loose on top.

e48c6e4d-d8c6-43dc-beb6-f43b51d2fc74.name: Salted Caramel Cheesecake Brownie Bars
e48c6e4d-d8c6-43dc-beb6-f43b51d2fc74.description: 9 x 120 | 13 p House calibration: sugar-substitutes → granulated Splenda (volume-matched); any light butter → real butter at matched calories. Imported via `batch ingest`.

steps.instructionText: Preheat oven to 350°F (175°C). Line an 8x8 inch baking pan with parchment paper.
For the brownie layer: In a large bowl, whisk together pumpkin purée, Greek yogurt, egg, egg whites, almond milk, and vanilla extract.
In a separate bowl, whisk together chocolate protein powder, cocoa powder, self-rising flour, sweetener, and salt.
Add the dry ingredients to the wet ingredients and mix until just combined. Do not overmix.
Spread the brownie batter evenly into the prepared baking pan.
For the cheesecake filling: In a medium bowl, beat together cream cheese, Greek yogurt, protein powder, egg, sweetener, and vanilla extract until smooth.
Carefully spoon the cheesecake filling over the brownie batter.
Bake for 25-30 minutes, or until the cheesecake is set. Let cool completely.
For the stovetop caramel topping: In a small saucepan, combine sugar-free caramel syrup, almond milk, sweetener, cornstarch, and sea salt.
Whisk constantly over medium heat until the mixture thickens, about 5-7 minutes. Remove from heat.
Pour the caramel topping over the cooled cheesecake layer and spread evenly.
Chill for at least 1 hour to set before cutting into bars.

slots.name: Torani sugar-free caramel syrup (or other brand)

notes.text: "Just combined" is critical here — this brownie layer has chocolate protein + cocoa + Greek yogurt + egg whites, all of which tighten fast when overmixed. Stop as soon as no dry flour streaks remain.
Bring the cream cheese and Greek yogurt to room temp before beating the cheesecake layer — cold dairy makes a lumpy filling that won't smooth out, and the lumps bake in permanently.
Don't beat air into the cheesecake layer — mix on low just until smooth. Airy cheesecake puffs in the oven, then cracks and sinks as it cools.

25–30 min is the window; pull when the cheesecake center has a slight wobble but isn't liquid — protein + Greek yogurt dry out fast past this point. The bars firm up fully only after cooling completely.

The Splenda-thickened caramel relies on cornstarch, not caramelization — if it's not thickening at 5 min, raise heat slightly and keep whisking. Stopping early leaves a watery sauce that soaks into the cheesecake.
Chill the full 1 hour before cutting — warm protein cheesecake is gummy and tears. For the cleanest slices, refrigerate overnight and run a warm dry knife between each cut.

99b26954-acc2-4bc6-9343-2e1e70de5bde.name: Sheet Pan Funfetti Snack Cake
99b26954-acc2-4bc6-9343-2e1e70de5bde.description: A high-protein, low-calorie sheet pan funfetti cake recipe that is easy to make and delicious. steps.instructionText: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Mix all ingredients in a large bowl.
Spray a 9x13 sheet pan with cooking spray and pour the batter in.
Bake for 35 minutes.
Let cool for 30 minutes.
Slice into 12 pieces and enjoy.

notes.text: 35 min is a guide for this specific 9x13 load — with 400 g Greek yogurt, 70 g whey, and 25 g coconut flour all pulling moisture at different rates, start checking at 28 min. A toothpick with moist crumbs (not wet batter) is done; overbaking turns the yogurt-heavy crumb rubbery.
Whisk the dry flours and protein together before adding wet — coconut flour (25 g) and whey clump badly if dropped into wet ingredients directly, leaving pockets that don't hydrate evenly.
Don't overmix once the eggs are in — the 3 whole eggs plus 180 g egg white is a lot of protein structure; overbeating develops it prematurely and makes the finished cake tight and tough.

The full 30-min cool is necessary before slicing — this cake is dense with yogurt and has no shortening to keep it tender warm. Cutting early gives gummy, tearing pieces that look underdone even when they aren't.
Cooking spray alone on a 9x13 may not be enough for a sticky protein batter — line with parchment after spraying, or the cake will stick at the corners and break when you lift slices.

9d2d47d2-7200-4087-a8b5-6420b01dc5b9.description: A simple protein cake with vanilla and Biscoff frosting — about 47 g protein per cake (4 servings ≈ 12 g protein, 116 cal each).
